items.title: US yield surge triggers mortgage hedging, adds to bond market pressure
items.author: Laura Matthews, Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
items.creator: Laura Matthews, Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
items.summary: The sharp rise in long-term US Treasury yields has spurred mortgage-related hedging that adds selling pressure to an already strained bond market, though the impact is likely smaller than in past selloffs.
items.body:
The sharp rise in long-term US Treasury yields has spurred mortgage-related hedging that adds selling pressure to an already strained bond market, though the impact is likely smaller than in past selloffs.
Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields have surged about 130 basis points and 30-year yields have climbed 100 basis points since late February, reflecting a war-driven oil-price spike that has kindled expectations for multiple Federal Reserve rate hikes over the next 12 months.
The rise in yields has pushed 30-year mortgage rates to a [USN:L1N45U0QE TEXT:"nearly three-year high of 7.4%"], keeping many homeowners locked into existing loans rather than refinancing as they often do when rates decline.
As rates rise, the expected life of mortgage-backed securities (MBS) extends, a shift that can make them more sensitive to further moves in yields. MBS investors often respond by either selling Treasury futures or by buying interest rate swaps that exchange a fixed coupon for a floating rate, a process known as "convexity hedging" that effectively reduces the duration of an asset.
"The market is carrying a substantial cohort of mortgages originated over the past three years at coupons relatively close to current mortgage rates," said Mike Riddle, chief executive officer at Eris Innovations, a Chicago-based futures and options products developer.
"If mortgage rates continue to climb and the possibility of further policy tightening remains, the expected duration of those loans can respond meaningfully to the next substantial move in rates," likely requiring additional hedging -- and additional selling pressure in Treasuries.
MBS are pools of thousands of home loans through which investors receive cash flows from homeowners' monthly principal and interest payments. Because these cash flows are affected by refinancing behavior, their risk profile shifts as interest rates change.
HEDGING ACTIVITY Evidence of that hedging activity has emerged in recent weeks across rates markets.
By the first week of October, nine megablock trades had been executed in CME-listed Eris swap futures tied to the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR), each carrying at least $200,000 of exposure to a 1 basis-point move in interest rates, Riddle said. The trades suggested that investors were adjusting positions to reflect shifts in the yield curve.
Daily volume in Eris SOFR Swap Futures hit consecutive records ahead of the Federal Reserve's September 16 policy meeting, including trades where investors repositioned for an expected rate increase. Open interest, or the number of outstanding contracts that have not been closed, climbed to a record 866,768 contracts on September 21, more than doubling the previous year's levels.
The activity has drawn attention because convexity hedging has often reinforced bond market selloffs.
The sharp underperformance of MBS and widening of mortgage spreads were also consistent with increased convexity hedging activity, analysts said. If MBS are performing particularly poorly relative to Treasuries at the same time that rates are moving sharply higher, that can be a sign that mortgage investors are hedging.
According to a recent research note from Annaly Capital Management (NLY.N) , one of the largest mortgage real estate investment trusts, MBS underperformed Treasuries with comparable duration by 96 basis points in September, their weakest monthly performance since the banking turmoil of March 2023.
MBS spreads to Treasuries also widened by about 13 basis points in September to 125 basis points, signaling that mortgages sold off more than government bonds, according to AGNC Investment Corp.
OUT OF THE MONEY Still, how much these hedging flows are contributing to the broader rise in yields remains an open question. Analysts say the effect tends to fade as yields rise because more mortgages become locked in, reducing their sensitivity to changes in interest rates.
"More and more of the MBS universe is significantly out of the money, which means they have no refinancing incentive and therefore no prepayment risk, which makes further selloffs less destabilizing," said Amrut Nashikkar, head of derivatives strategy at Barclays.
Neil Sun, a portfolio manager at BlueBay Asset Management, said that if rates stabilize at their current levels, the biggest selling pressure may be in the rearview mirror.
Beyond cyclical factors, the mortgage market itself is no longer large enough to exert the same influence on Treasury yields it once did, analysts said.
James Wang, head of macro at US Bank, said the mortgage market is much smaller than the one that amplified bond market swings before the 2008 financial crisis.
The mortgage portfolios of the government-sponsored housing enterprises Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac have contracted significantly since the crisis. Fannie and Freddie were the biggest hedgers pre-crisis because they actively managed the duration gap, reflecting interest-rate risk, between their assets and liabilities.
"At the end of the day, monetary policy expectations are the No. 1 driver of the selloff," Wang said.

items.title: Huracán Simón deja al menos un muerto e inundaciones
items.author: Alberto Fajardo, Daniel Becerril
items.creator: Alberto Fajardo, Daniel Becerril
items.summary: El huracán Simon avanzaba lentamente el lunes hacia el oeste frente a la costa del Pacífico mexicano, azotando estados del occidente del país con fuertes vientos y lluvias que ha, dejado al menos un muerto, inundaciones y cientos de personas desalojadas.
items.body:
El huracán Simon avanzaba lentamente el lunes hacia el oeste frente a la costa del Pacífico mexicano, azotando estados del occidente del país con fuertes vientos y lluvias que ha, dejado al menos un muerto, inundaciones y cientos de personas desalojadas.
La directora de Protección Civil de México, Laura Velázquez, informó el lunes que una persona falleció el fin de semana en el estado Guerrero, donde se encuentra el popular destino turístico de Acapulco, debido a la tormenta, aunque no dio detalles.
El Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC por su sigla en inglés) informó en su reporte más reciente que Simon se encontraba a unos 95 kilómetros al oeste-suroeste de Cabo Corrientes, en el estado Jalisco, con vientos máximos sostenidos de 165 kilómetros por hora (km/h) y moviéndose lentamente a 4 km/h.
Simon, un huracán de categoría 2, se ha debilitado desde el sábado, cuando alcanzó la categoría 4.
"Simon está perdiendo intensidad de viento poco a poco y podría estancarse esta semana", dijo Alex DaSilva, experto en huracanes de la firma privada de pronósticos meteorológicos AccuWeather.
"Cuanto más lento se mueva Simon, mayor será el potencial de lluvia que traerá la tormenta, pero ahora mismo la mayor parte de esa lluvia se encuentra mar adentro y al sur del centro de la tormenta", añadió.
Autoridades mexicanas advirtieron que Simon podría provocar inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra potencialmente mortales en algunas zonas de la costa del Pacífico y en zonas montañosas cercanas.
Los efectos de Simon se suman a los de la tormenta Rachel en Baja Califormia, que el fin de semana dejó una menor muerta por inundaciones, dijo el lunes la gobernadora de ese estado, Marina del Pilar Ávila, quien añadió que al menos 10 personas permanecía desaparecidas en el municipio Ensenada.
El NHC dijo que se prevé que Simon retome un movimiento lento hacia el noroeste la noche del lunes para posteriormente dar un giro gradual hacia el noreste y que Simon se acerque a la costa centro-occidental de México entre el miércoles y el jueves y que se mantenga como huracán hasta mediados de semana.
Estima que dejará entre cinco y 10 centímetros de lluvia en zonas costeras del suroeste y centro-oeste de México, con acumulaciones aisladas de entre 15 y 20 centímetros en partes de Jalisco y Sinaloa. Las acumulaciones aisladas podrían alcanzar 76 centímetros en partes de Michoacán, Colima y Jalisco, dijo el NHC.
En la localidad costera Cihuatlán, al suroeste de Jalisco, las patrullas alertaron a los residentes sobre una posible evacuación debido a la crecida del río Marabasco. Durante la noche, el agua anegó las calles y las zonas bajas de la ciudad.
En la ciudad portuaria Manzanillo, en el estado Colima, los residentes caminaban por casas y calles inundadas mientras marinos ayudaba a drenar el agua.
"Todo se inundó", dijo la residente María Elena Vázquez desde el interior de su casa, con los pantalones remangados mientras el agua le llegaba hasta los tobillos.
El CNH indicó que se esperaba que Simón produjera marejadas ciclónicas peligrosas y olas destructivas de gran tamaño cerca de la costa. También se pronostica que el oleaje provocado por el huracán generará condiciones de resaca y oleaje peligroso en el suroeste y centro-oeste de México durante los próximos días.

items.title: Nasdaq cae mientras petróleo se dispara a la espera de resultados empresariales, datos económicos
items.author: Ragini Mathur, Purvi Agarwal
items.creator: Ragini Mathur, Purvi Agarwal
items.summary: El Nasdaq cerró en baja el lunes, después de que el petróleo subió casi 2 dólares por barril tras los ataques contra un aeropuerto saudita, mientras los inversores esperan que los bancos den el pistoletazo de salida a la temporada de resultados del tercer trimestre y a los datos económicos de esta semana.
items.body:
El Nasdaq cerró en baja el lunes, después de que el petróleo subió casi 2 dólares por barril tras los ataques contra un aeropuerto saudita, mientras los inversores esperan que los bancos den el pistoletazo de salida a la temporada de resultados del tercer trimestre y a los datos económicos de esta semana.
El S&P 500 cerró prácticamente sin cambios, mientras que el Dow Jones subió.
El petróleo subió, ya que los ataques contra Arabia Saudita pesaron más que la perspectiva de un aumento de la oferta, a pesar de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, celebró las nuevas exportaciones rusas de diésel y el alto el fuego entre Rusia y Ucrania en materia de objetivos energéticos.
La atención del mercado se centra ahora en los resultados empresariales, ya que se espera que los beneficios del S&P 500 se disparen un 30,6% en el tercer trimestre, según datos de LSEG IBES.
Los principales bancos estadounidenses, entre ellos Goldman Sachs (GS.N) , Citigroup (C.N) y JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) , darán el pistoletazo de salida a la temporada de resultados el martes.
También se publicarán esta semana las cifras de septiembre sobre la inflación de los precios al consumo y al productor en Estados Unidos, así como los datos de ventas al por menor.
Según los datos preliminares de cierre, el S&P 500 (.SPX) perdió 3,75 puntos, o un 0,05%, a 7.807,79 puntos; mientras que el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) cedió 120,17 puntos, o un 0,44%, a 27.246,00 unidades. El Dow Jones (.DJI) subió 198,22 puntos, o un 0,38%, a 51.853,17 unidades.
Con el aumento de los precios del petróleo, el sector energético (.SPNY) superó en rendimiento a los principales sectores industriales del S&P 500. El índice de servicios de comunicación del S&P 500 (.SPLRCL) también subió, impulsado por Meta (META.O) .
Los sectores de tecnología (.SPLRCT) y consumo discrecional (.SPLRCD) fueron los más rezagados. La debilidad del sector tecnológico fue más pronunciada entre las acciones de chips, ya que el índice de semiconductores de Filadelfia (.SOX) perdió terreno y alcanzó su mínimo en tres semanas.
Salesforce (CRM.N) subió tras una doble revisión al alza de BofA Global Research, que pasó de "rendimiento inferior al mercado" a "comprar", lo que impulsó al Dow a su máximo en casi tres semanas.
En el sector de consumo discrecional, las acciones de Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG.N) cayeron después de que Starbucks (SBUX.O) anunciara que no iba a adquirir la cadena de burritos.
Microsoft (MSFT.O) subió luego de que su capitalización bursátil superara los 4 billones de dólares por primera vez en un año tras anunciar planes para un importante despliegue de sus propios chips de IA.

PARIS, Oct 12 : Hackers forced the temperature of many French supermarket fridges up to 50 degrees Celsius (122°F) overnight, causing fires and food losses at several hundred stores across the country in a major cyberattack.
The Paris prosecutor's office said a "large-scale" attack was "affecting connected refrigerators in several major food retailers across France" and reported damage included "food losses and fires".
Meanwhile, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu instructed France's National Cybersecurity Agency ANSSI to investigate, a person in his office said.
They said France "was coordinating with its European counterparts, as other countries may also be affected," while also investigating whether any other French firms were at risk.

Les Mousquetaires, which owns retailer Intermarche, said around 150 of its stores had been hit, with fridges heated up to 50 degrees Celsius for six hours. It had thrown all the food away to avoid any sanitary risks, a spokesperson said.
And Cooperative U CEO Dominique Schelcher said his supermarket had also been hit by the attack.
"Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented," he wrote on X.
Carrefour said 80 of its supermarkets had been hit but that the vast majority of its 6,000 stores had not been affected. 
Several other supermarket chains, including Monoprix, E.Leclerc and Auchan, did not respond to requests for comment.
DUTCH SECURITY ISSUE
Dutch supermarket operator Ahold Delhaize, which operates the Netherlands' largest supermarket chain Albert Heijn and has substantial operations in the United States, said it was also dealing with a "security issue" in its network, and had taken several systems offline to protect them.
A smartphone app for the retailer told clients that due to a "cybersecurity incident" it was unable to deliver groceries.
Online orders represent around 10 per cent of sales for Albert Heijn. Physical stores remained open and Dutch news agency ANP reported that rivals had seen an influx of delivery orders.
It was not clear if there was any link between the French supermarket attack and the problems flagged by Ahold Delhaize. 
Ahold is the fourth-largest grocery retailer in the US, where websites for its Stop & Shop, Giant, Hannaford and Food Lion stores all had notices saying "site temporarily down".
It was unclear if other operations were affected.
The source close to Lecornu said ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in software supplied by Danish company Danfoss.
Danfoss said it was "aware of incidents in France affecting a limited number of refrigeration management systems".

items.title: Hackers heat French supermarket fridges, sparking fires and spoiling food
items.author: Leo Marchandon, Gabriel Stargardter
items.creator: Leo Marchandon, Gabriel Stargardter
items.summary: Hackers raised the temperature of refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, causing fires and spoiling food.
items.body:
Hackers raised the temperature of refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, causing fires and spoiling food.
The Paris prosecutor's office said on Monday that a "large-scale" attack was "affecting connected refrigerators in several major food retailers across France", leading to food losses and fires.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has instructed France's National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) to investigate, a person in his office said.
France was coordinating with European counterparts because other countries could also be affected, the person said, adding that authorities were assessing whether other French companies were at risk.
Felix Aime, a senior cyber threat intelligence analyst at Sekoia Threat Detection and Research, said Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium had also been affected.
Carrefour (CARR.PA) said 80 of its supermarkets were hit, while Monoprix, which operates about 490 stores in France, said 5% of its stores were affected.
Les Mousquetaires, owner of retailer Intermarche, said fridges at around 150 of its stores were heated up to 50 C for six hours overnight. A spokesperson said all affected food had been discarded to eliminate health risks.
Paris resident Geert de Clercq witnessed staff at an Intermarche in central Paris throwing cartfuls of defrosted frozen foods into a giant trash container, with molten ice cream sloshing out of broken tubs on the street.
Cooperative U CEO Dominique Schelcher said his supermarket group had also been targeted.
"Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented," he wrote on X.
Food retailers E.Leclerc and Auchan did not respond to requests for comment.
There was no immediate estimate of industry-wide losses, but Intermarche CEO Thierry Cotillard told BFM TV the "unprecedented" attack would represent losses amounting to "tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day."
Christel Delberghe, director general at European retail association Eurocommerce, said, "This incident underlines the importance of resilience across the entire supply chain."
COLD AISLES CONTROLLED OVER INTERNET Supermarket cold aisles are typically run by control panels that manage an entire store's fridges and freezers and can be accessed over the internet, which lets maintenance companies adjust them from anywhere.
The source close to Lecornu said ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in software supplied by Danish company Danfoss.
Danfoss said it was "aware of incidents in France affecting a limited number of refrigeration management systems".
The affected units "were running outdated firmware", Danfoss said, adding that it had "long advised customers to keep supported systems updated with the latest firmware and to migrate legacy systems to current-generation solutions".
On August 9, cybersecurity firm Claroty's Team82 published research detailing vulnerabilities in the Danfoss AK-SM 800A controller. According to the report, software updates issued by Danfoss addressed issues that could have allowed attackers to bypass authentication controls and execute code on compromised devices.
The attacks resemble disruptions reported at about a dozen US military commissaries in late August that led to food losses after fridges were affected.
In a statement, French retail association Fédération du Commerce et de la Distribution called for "full transparency" from Danfoss about the incident. It said supermarkets aimed to protect consumers and return to normal operations as soon as possible. The FCD said some impacted stores were already back up and running.
DUTCH SECURITY ISSUE Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize (AD.AS) , which operates the Netherlands' largest supermarket chain Albert Heijn and has major operations in the US, said it was dealing with a "security issue" on its network and had taken several systems offline as a precaution.
A message on the retailer's smartphone app said it was unable to deliver groceries because of a "cybersecurity incident".
Online orders account for about 10% of Albert Heijn sales. Physical stores remained open, while Dutch news agency ANP reported that rival retailers had seen a surge in delivery orders.
Ahold Delhaize said there was no reason to see a link between the incidents in France and its supermarkets.
Ahold is the fourth-largest grocery retailer in the US. Websites for its Stop & Shop, Giant, Hannaford and Food Lion chains displayed notices saying "site temporarily down".
It was unclear whether other operations had been affected.

items.title: Hurricane Simon crawls along Mexico's Pacific coast, bringing floods and evacuations
items.author: Alberto Fajardo, Daniel Becerril
items.creator: Alberto Fajardo, Daniel Becerril
items.summary: Hurricane Simon crept northwest just off Mexico's Pacific coast on Monday, lashing western states with dangerous winds, heavy rain and flooding that put riverside communities on alert for possible evacuations.
items.body:
Hurricane Simon crept northwest just off Mexico's Pacific coast on Monday, lashing western states with dangerous winds, heavy rain and flooding that put riverside communities on alert for possible evacuations.
The US National Hurricane Center said Simon was about 55 miles (90 km) west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes in Jalisco state at 8 a.m. (1400 GMT), packing maximum sustained winds of 110 mph (175 kph), making it a Category 2 hurricane.
Simon has weakened since Saturday when it was a Category 4 system.
"Simon is slowly losing wind intensity and could ultimately stall this week and never make a true landfall as an organized storm," said Alex DaSilva, a hurricane expert at private forecaster AccuWeather.
Simon is forecast to make landfall on Thursday in Mexico's Sinaloa state.
"The slower Simon moves, the more rain potential the storm carries, but right now most of that rain is offshore and to the south of the storm's center ultimately sparing the feet of rain we thought this storm could initially bring," said DaSilva.
Simon was moving northwest at just 3 mph (6 kph) and was expected to continue along that track before turning northeast and moving inland across west-central Mexico around midweek.
Authorities said that Simon could bring life-threatening flooding and mudslides to parts of the Pacific coast and nearby mountains.
The hurricane is forecast to dump an additional 2 to 4 inches (5 to 10 cm) of rain across coastal areas of southwest and west-central Mexico, with isolated amounts of 6 to 8 inches (15 to 20 cm) in parts of Jalisco and Sinaloa. The National Hurricane Center said isolated storm totals could reach 30 inches (76 cm) in parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco.
The head of Mexico's civil protection agency, Laura Velazquez, said one person was reported to have died due to the storm in Guerrero state, home to the popular tourist destination of Acapulco.
In the coastal town of Cihuatlan in southwestern Jalisco, patrols warned residents to prepare for potential evacuation as the Marabasco River rose. Floodwater inundated streets and low-lying areas of the town overnight.
In the port city of Manzanillo in Colima state, residents waded through flooded homes and streets as navy personnel helped remove water.
"Everything got flooded," said resident Maria Elena Vazquez from inside her home, pants rolled up as the water came up to her ankles.
The National Hurricane Center said Simon was expected to produce dangerous storm surge and large destructive waves close to where it approaches the coast. Swells from the hurricane are also forecast to create life-threatening surf and rip current conditions along southwestern and west-central Mexico over the next few days.
Following weeks of storms that have battered Mexico, at least 10 people are missing in the state of Baja California and one minor was killed in the coastal city of Ensenada.

LONDON, Oct 12 : Britain's AI Security Institute has been given access to the latest advanced AI models and is working with the US government and major developers, including Google, to assess their safety, AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said on Monday.
Britain, which is not home to any major AI developers, is seeking a leading role in efforts to assess and manage the risks posed by increasingly powerful AI systems.
Scrutiny of AI safety has intensified after developers including Anthropic and OpenAI disclosed instances of rogue or undesired behaviour by AI agents. Some industry figures have warned the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity.
Monday's announcement, which did not specify all the models the institute is evaluating, comes after reports last month that the White House has asked OpenAI and Anthropic to withhold new models from British testers pending a US review.

"I can confirm that AI scientists at the AI Security Institute are now conducting rigorous evaluations of the latest generation of models, including Gemini 4 Argon, to identify risks early, to test robust safeguards, to help keep people safe," Narayan said.
Under voluntary agreements with major AI developers, the institute receives access to models before deployment, allowing it to assess their capabilities and risks and contribute to emerging international safety standards.
Microsoft President Brad Smith said in an interview published by the BBC on Monday that Britain was well placed to help lead work on AI safety guidelines.
In a letter published in September, the AISI said Anthropic had made clear that no organisation outside the US had access to its Mythos 5.1 model.
Asked about access to frontier AI systems — something ministers have never confirmed the institute had lost on a wider basis — Narayan said the government had a long-standing relationship with the US built on trust.
"When you're reliant on someone else's technology, you have to be clear-eyed about the permanence of any outcome. But I'm very confident that, as a consequence of the conversations we've had, we will be able to test the latest generation of models," he said.

items.title: Starbucks says not buying Chipotle, ends takeover speculation
items.author: Anuja Mistry, Neil Kanatt
items.creator: Anuja Mistry, Neil Kanatt
items.summary: Starbucks is not buying Chipotle Mexican Grill , the coffee chain said on Monday, quashing talk of a deal that could have been the largest-ever involving restaurants but was doubted by both investors and analysts.
items.body:
Starbucks (SBUX.O) is not buying Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG.N) , the coffee chain said on Monday, quashing talk of a deal that could have been the largest-ever involving restaurants but was doubted by both investors and analysts.
"As a matter of policy, we don't comment on rumors and speculation, but we want to be clear we are not buying Chipotle," a Starbucks spokesperson said. Chipotle declined to comment.
The statement follows [USN:L6N45U0YK TEXT:"a report by the Financial Times on October 8"] that Starbucks had worked with advisers in recent months on a potential proposal to acquire Chipotle, citing people familiar with the matter.
Starbucks did not respond to a request for comment on whether they approached advisers for a deal.
Shares of the coffee chain were up 1% in early trading, while Chipotle, whose shares surged on the prospect of a takeover which would have reunited Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol with the burrito chain he led for six years, fell about 4%.
Starbucks also reiterated that its management was "laser focused" on "Back to Starbucks" strategy and had "strong momentum and confidence" in its long-term growth prospects. The company aims to share its fourth-quarter results and fiscal 2027 outlook later this month.
Starbucks shares have gained 7.8% this year, roughly half the gain in the S&P 500 over the period. The chain has been closing [USN:L4N45G0UG TEXT:"dozens"] of underperforming stores as part of a turnaround led by Niccol, who has tried to draw back customers with shorter wait times and simpler menus.
TAKEOVER SPECULATION The report of a potential deal last week prompted the investor community to speculate about a tie-up that would have brought together two of the largest US restaurant brands.
Chances of a deal sent Chipotle shares up more than 7% and Starbucks down about 3%, even as several analysts questioned the strategic rationale as Starbucks was in revival mode under Niccol.
"Rumors like these can prime investment bankers to start fantasizing about all sorts of tie-ups, but they're a tough sell. The tide has been shifting more toward divestitures than acquisitions," From Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management said.
A potential deal would have created a restaurant giant with about $50 billion in annual sales, positioning it to better navigate uncertain demand from inflation-hit consumers, rising operating costs and the squeeze on profits. The burrito chain has a market capitalization is around $40 billion.
NICCOL'S CHALLENGE "Funding a premium takeover price would likely require a mix of debt and equity, which would test leverage and could dilute existing shareholders while Starbucks is still executing its turnaround," Paren Knadjian, Partner at Transaction Advisory Services, EisnerAmper said last week.
Niccol joined Starbucks in 2024 after leading Chipotle through a period of rapid growth and digital expansion.
He was credited with reviving the burrito chain after its food-safety crises and expanding its digital business, helping accelerate sales growth.
Chipotle, meanwhile, has grappled with softer traffic as consumers cut back spending, while higher food and labor costs hurt margins across the restaurant industry. Their shares have nearly halved in value since Niccol's departure.

「イエメン問題は（国連の）ロードマップ（行程表）によってずっと前に解決しているべきだった。われわれは、イエメンとサウジの間で成立するいかなる合意も支持すると表明していた」とし、対話を通じた解決を望むと述べた。

Oct 12 : Global smartphone shipments fell 20 per cent on-year to their lowest third-quarter level since 2012, as soaring memory chip costs and supply shortages pressured manufacturers and pushed up prices, preliminary estimates from Counterpoint Research showed on Monday.
Rising prices for memory components as AI infrastructure projects corner supplies have driven up production costs and prompted manufacturers to raise retail prices, cut shipments and prioritize profitability over volumes.
"Consumers are holding on to their devices longer than estimated, increasingly considering refurbished devices and prioritizing higher-value devices," said Counterpoint senior analyst Shilpi Jain.
Samsung retained its top position with a 23 per cent market share, helped by demand for its Galaxy Z Fold8 series and stable component supplies for its mid-range devices. Shipments fell 3 per cent from a year earlier during the quarter.

OPPO and vivo recorded shipment declines of more than 20 per cent. Xiaomi saw a more than 30 per cent fall, reducing its market share to 10 per cent as the company cut exposure to lower-priced devices and some overseas markets to protect margins.
"The outlook for the remainder of 2026 remains challenging," Counterpoint said.

items.title: サウジ首都の空港が閉鎖延長、フーシ派攻撃で被害　経済への影響懸念
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Gianluca Lo Nostro　Menna AlaaElDin

［１２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Gianluca Lo Nostro　Menna AlaaElDin

［１２日　ロイター］ - サウジアラビア当局は１２日、週末にイエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派の攻撃を受けた首都リヤドのキング・ハリド国際空港の運用停止措置を１７日まで延長した。

サウジ民間航空当局は、空港閉鎖について、「空港施設の安全と運用準備態勢を確保するための手続きを完了させる」ためだと説明した。同空港の利用者数は、ジッダに次いで国内２番目に多い。

フーシ派は１２日夜、弾道ミサイルで同空港を攻撃したと発表した。これに先立ち、サウジ側は、フーシ派がリヤドに向けて発射した弾道ミサイルを迎撃・破壊したと発表していた。

フーシ派は声明で、サウジ南西部ハミスムシャイトの空軍基地もドローン（無人機）で攻撃したと表明した。これについてサウジ側は現時点で確認していない。

１２日に発出された航空情報（ＮＯＴＡＭ）によると、キング・ハリド国際空港は１０月１７日２１００ＧＭＴ（日本時間１８日午前６時）まで閉鎖される。

同空港は１０日の攻撃以降、閉鎖されている。この攻撃では１３人が死亡、３００人超が負傷し、サウジ国内では過去１０年以上で最も多くの死者を出した。１１日の別の攻撃では１人が死亡し、十数人が負傷した。

一連の攻撃は、サウジ航空業界に混乱をもたらすとともに、航空燃料の高騰に直面している航空会社にさらなる打撃となっている。

航空機追跡サイト「フライトレーダー２４」のデータによると、航空機は１２日、リヤドを避けて飛行している。ただ、サウジ領空を通過し、西海岸の主要拠点であるジッダに着陸する便は見られた。

航空データ分析会社シリウムによると、サウジ国内の全空港での欠航率は４６．４％に達した。

混乱を受けて欧州やアジアの航空各社は運航停止を余儀なくされている。欧州航空安全庁（ＥＡＳＡ）は９日、ミサイルやドローンによる攻撃を理由に、サウジ領空に関する警告の対象範囲を拡大した。米連邦航空局（ＦＡＡ）は１１日、米国の航空会社に対し、サウジへの飛行や領空通過の際に警戒するよう勧告した。

ルフトハンザ・グループはリヤド便を１０月１６日まで全便欠航とし、エールフランスＫＬＭはリヤド発着便の運航停止措置を今月末まで延長した。

アブダビのエティハド航空もサウジ便の欠航延長を決めた。

デルタ航空は、当初１０月２３日に予定していたアトランタ─リヤド線の就航を２０２７年３月まで延期すると発表した。

今回の攻撃は、今月リヤドで開催予定の大規模会合にも影を落とす。世界石油会議（ＷＰＣ）の会合は、複数の石油大手トップが参加を取りやめた。

フーシ派との衝突激化により、より広範な経済的影響への懸念が強まっている。サウジの実質国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）は、石油活動の低迷など複数の要因を反映し、２０２６年に３．６％縮小すると予測されている。

items.title: Saudi Arabia faces new missile and drone fire after major attacks on airports
items.author: Timour Azhari
items.creator: Timour Azhari
items.summary: Saudi Arabia said it was facing a new barrage of incoming fire on Monday and that Riyadh airport would remain shut for now, days after Saturday's deadly missile strike on a departure terminal that was claimed by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis.
items.body:
Saudi Arabia said it was facing a new barrage of incoming fire on Monday and that Riyadh airport would remain shut for now, days after Saturday's deadly [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"missile strike"] on a departure terminal that was claimed by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis.
Incoming drones and missiles were reported by the Saudi-led coalition backing government forces in Yemen, though there was no immediate news of whether they were intercepted.
The [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"Houthis"] have been attacking Saudi airports and oil facilities since last week as part of a rapidly escalating conflict that has spilled over from the wider regional conflagration between the United States and Iran .
Those attacks have shut down parts of Saudi airspace, [USN:L6N45Y0C1 TEXT:"suspending operations"] at Riyadh airport, and largely emptying the skies over the capital even as the city hosts a major [USN:L6N45Y0GT TEXT:"energy conference"].
Saudi Arabia now faces a nightmare predicament, having [USN:L1N45Q02D TEXT:"re-entered Yemen's civil war"] to push the Houthis from the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait oil route and stop the group making further gains after its sudden advances in September.
With the Yemeni forces Riyadh supports having made some gains against the Houthis around Bab el-Mandeb but still on the back foot on other fronts, Yemeni military sources said, any pressure on the Houthis could take time to pay off.
Saudi Arabia's long-time regional rival Iran offered to mediate between its Houthi allies and the kingdom. "We have repeatedly expressed our readiness to help facilitate dialogue between the parties," foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said on Monday.
Meanwhile, despite intensified Saudi airstrikes against the group, including what Yemeni television said were hits on al-Jawf province on Monday, the Houthis show no sign of letting up their own barrage of attacks on Saudi infrastructure.
The group has repeatedly threatened to target airports and airspace, as well as Saudi oil installations that provide the engine for the kingdom's economy and its ambitious development plans.
UAE CALLS FOR JOINT GULF ACTION Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said at Monday's conference that the kingdom would stay focused on bringing in investment as part of its wider economic development goals.
"The development of our energy system and industrial capability continues," he said.
Saudi Arabia's neighbour the United Arab Emirates on Monday called for a revival of joint Gulf action on security and defence in response to the attacks. UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said the targeting of Saudi Arabia undermined the security of all Gulf states and added that the neglect of collective Gulf security had "emboldened others" to overreach against regional states.
Saudi Arabia and the UAE had been partners in the Yemen conflict for years, but they backed different forces within the Yemeni military coalition supporting the government and fell out last winter.
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that Washington was considering joining Saudi Arabia in strikes on the Houthis, but there has been no sign yet of any US action.

items.title: Microsoft plans huge deployment of its own AI chips, with an eye on saving costs
items.author: Stephen Nellis, Max Cherney
items.creator: Stephen Nellis, Max Cherney
items.summary: Microsoft announced the next generation of its custom AI chip on Monday and said it plans to deploy potentially more than a million of them next year to back its internal AI services.
items.body:
Microsoft (MSFT.O) announced the next generation of its custom AI chip on Monday and said it plans to deploy potentially more than a million of them next year to back its internal AI services.
The Maia 300, as the chip is called, is the third generation of the company's custom chips designed to handle AI data crunching such as coding and carrying out complex business tasks on a user's behalf. Its predecessor is already running Microsoft's in-house AI models, as well as models from OpenAI delivered on Microsoft's Azure cloud computing service.
The new version comes amid a flurry of custom chips from both [USN:L6N45G0UZ TEXT:"cloud computing rivals"] and [USN:L6N42V15J TEXT:"AI firms such as OpenAI"] aimed at loosening the hold of Nvidia (NVDA.O) on the AI computing market.
To construct the chip, Microsoft took a different technical path from Nvidia whose AI accelerators use one massive computing chip surrounded by high-bandwidth memory chips.
The central computing processor in Microsoft's Maia 300 silicon is composed of "chiplets" — typically specialized chips bonded together — that use 2-nanometer technology from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (2330.TW) for key computing functions.
Other chiplets included in the design use cheaper 3-nanometer tech for functions such as moving data off the processor and elsewhere inside the system.
The Maia 300 processors will go into racks that contain 96 chips and use about 167 kilowatts of power, compared with the 142 kilowatts used by Nvidia's most recent GB300 AI server racks with 72 of its graphics processing units (GPUs).
Microsoft said the Maia 300 chips will get about 40% more useful computing done per megawatt than "leading GPU-based systems," though it did not name the systems it used for a comparison.
"It's basically delivering more intelligence for every watt, every dollar, and every byte of memory by optimizing across the entire system," Rani Borkar, president of Azure hardware systems and infrastructure at Microsoft, told Reuters in an interview.
Microsoft said it plans to roll out "multi-gigawatt deployments" of the Maia 300 chip starting next year. Microsoft has said it [USN:L4N43V23K TEXT:"expects to spend"] more than $175 billion in capital expenditures this calendar year.

items.title: Wall Street’s AI bet is now too big to hit
items.author: Jamie McGeever
items.creator: Jamie McGeever
items.summary: The hurdle for continued AI-driven equity gains is strikingly high. And with cracks starting to appear in the seemingly impenetrable tech edifice, there are mounting signs AI risk is now far more than just a case of "bad vibes."
items.body:
The hurdle for continued AI-driven equity gains is strikingly high. And with cracks starting to appear in the seemingly impenetrable tech edifice, there are mounting signs AI risk is now far more than just a case of "bad vibes."
While the S&P 500 (.SPX) and Nasdaq (.IXIC) climbed to fresh highs last week, a string of negative headlines related to AI – from a shelved initial public offering (IPO) in Australia to reports that ChatGPT maker OpenAI's revenue is [USN:L4N45U1QQ TEXT:"falling short"] of earlier estimates – suggests markets could soon run into some serious obstacles.
Earnings releases and forecasts from the big AI players in the coming weeks may ease those concerns. But the bar is high – very high. Analysts expect S&P 500 earnings to rise more than 30% year-over-year for the third quarter, with two-thirds of that coming from tech and AI, according to Tajinder Dhillon, LSEG's head of earnings and equity research. Some analysts say up to 80% of the anticipated increase in total profit growth from S&P 500 companies will come from this one area.
Investors are right to be cautious.
On Friday, Australia's [USN:P8N42P0IJ TEXT:"Firmus"], a data center operator backed by Nvidia (NVDA.O) , shelved its $5 billion IPO. It would have been the country's second-largest initial share sale ever, and the fourth largest globally this year.
That was obviously a negative twist, but even positive news from AI firms may not be good enough. On Thursday, South Korea's [USN:P8N44T045 TEXT:"Samsung"] (005930.KS) , the world's largest memory chipmaker, said it expects to announce third-quarter earnings of around $80 billion, which would be a record quarterly profit for any tech company.
On the same day, Taiwan's [USN:P8N3NB03R TEXT:"TSMC "] (2330.TW) , the world's largest contract chipmaker, reported record third-quarter revenue of $46.7 billion, beating forecasts and rising 50% from a year earlier. Yet shares in both companies fell.
Of course, isolated share price moves and company-specific announcements aren't indicative of the trajectory of a multi-trillion-dollar industry.
But they are part of a steady drip of less-than-stellar headlines. Let's not forget, it also emerged last week that [USN:L4N45U1QQ TEXT:"OpenAI's annualized revenue"] for September was around $50 billion, down $20 billion from previous indications.
This all suggests the bigger AI picture could face some seriously harsh scrutiny this earnings season.
THE HIGHEST BAR The sums being spent on the AI revolution, and therefore those required to make it profitable, are eye-watering.
The total cost of financing the AI buildout from last year to 2032 is estimated at $10.3 trillion, or an average of 3.63% of US gross domestic product per year, according to Columbia University professor Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh .
Assuming a conservative 10% return — below the 15-20% return on investment many analysts say AI investment is targeting — Van Nieuwerburgh estimates the annual revenue required "to recover the investment, replace depreciating capital, and compensate investors for the opportunity cost of capital" is around $3.55 trillion by 2032.
That's more than 9% of GDP, roughly what Americans spend on motor vehicles, transport, household furnishings, clothes, and energy combined. When you consider that annual combined revenue of OpenAI and Anthropic is currently around $100 billion, total revenue would need to grow more than 80% a year through 2032 to get to the required $3.55 trillion total, Van Nieuwerburgh says.
"If the economic life of IT equipment is shorter, the revenue requirement rises substantially," he said.
BIGGEST MISALLOCATION EVER? AI and tech firms' profits have, so far, mostly met Wall Street’s soaring expectations. Can they continue to do so?
JPMorgan Private Bank's Michael Cembalest says AI-related stocks, which he narrows down to 41 names, have accounted for 75% of S&P 500 returns, 80% of earnings growth and 90% of capital spending growth since ChatGPT launched in November 2022. That’s an extraordinarily heavy burden for so few companies.
The outlooks provided by the CEOs and CFOs of these 41 firms in the coming weeks could indicate whether a market correction could be on the horizon – and just how large it could be.
AI is far and away the biggest investment boom in US history. Could it also end up being the biggest misallocation of capital?
(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters)

What Trump’s Russian diesel deal means for US, surging global prices & Indian refiners

The US has eased sanctions on Russian diesel to address fuel-price pressures, raising questions over its Russia policy and the outlook for Indian refiners.

Udit Bubna

12 October, 2026 06:27 pm IST

Facebook

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-

New Delhi: US President Donald Trump’s decision to bring Russian diesel back into the American market has raised questions about Washington’s sanctions policy against Moscow and its efforts to curb revenues funding the war in Ukraine.

Trump’s decision comes ahead of the November mid-term elections, with diesel prices near record levels. Diesel is essential for trucking, agriculture and heating in the US, making higher fuel costs a concern for households and businesses.

The announcement on Friday came less than a month after Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which provides for tariffs of up to 100 percent on goods from countries that continue to buy Russian oil and gas under specified conditions.

Show Full Article

On 9 October, the US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued General License 135, temporarily authorising specified transactions involving Russian-origin diesel until 7 April 2027, allowing the proposed trade to proceed.

However, analysts are sceptical that the additional volumes will significantly ease global diesel shortages or bring down prices across markets.

Abu Dhabi-based commodity analyst Natalia Katona said the arrangement appeared to be directed at a specific regional market rather than the global diesel shortage. “The US Atlantic coast, particularly New York and the wider Northeast, has a persistent diesel shortfall because it lacks sufficient refining capacity.” .

Regular seaborne imports of around 200,000-300,000 barrels per day help meet that shortfall, Katona said.

“While many in the market argue that these volumes won’t solve the global diesel shortage, Trump is addressing a very specific local problem: diesel prices in the traditionally Democratic Northeast ahead of the elections,” she told ThePrint.

Also Read: India’s now importing pre-conflict levels of Gulf crude; share of Russian oil lowest since April

Sanctions relief versus pressure on Russia
Trump’s move highlights the contrast between the US easing restrictions on its own proposed Russian diesel imports and threatening penalties against other major buyers of Russian energy.

America-based energy strategist and geopolitical analyst Umud Shokri said the arrangement was administratively permitted under the US licence, but actual deliveries would depend on available Russian supplies, export rules, shipping and payment arrangements. He also noted that some US lawmakers had questioned whether the move conflicted with federal law.

Russia’s own restrictions could pose another constraint. Moscow extended its diesel export ban for producers until 31 October, citing the need to stabilise domestic fuel supplies. Meanwhile, Ukrainian drone attacks continue to disrupt Russian refining capacity.

Despite restrictions on diesel exports, Russia continued supplying some foreign markets during the sanctions period through government-to-government arrangements which was exempt from its export ban, Katona said. These shipments included supplies to Mongolia, Kyrgyzstan and other Central Asian countries.

Shokri said there was no indication that Russian refineries returned to peak operating levels. In September, half of Russia’s six largest diesel-producing refineries had significantly reduced or halted output following drone damage, he said.

Under Trump’s supply arrangement, Russia is expected to ship 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and one million tonnes in December, according to Katona.

These volumes would be equivalent to around 75,000 barrels per day (b/d), 125,000 b/d and 250,000 b/d, respectively, averaged over a month. The December shipment could cover almost all of the US Northeast’s regular diesel import requirement of 200,000-300,000 b/d.

However, high freight rates and a shortage of clean-product tankers could limit the wider impact, as diesel markets have become increasingly regional.

Russia, according to Katona, last supplied diesel to the US in 2022, with arrivals peaking at 210,000 tonnes in December that year. No cargoes have arrived since 2023.

What it means for India’s oil trade
For Indian refiners, the bigger risk lies in changing regional trade flows and potential pressure on export margins rather than direct competition from Russian diesel in the US.

India exported 630,000 barrels per day (b/d) of diesel in September, of which Europe took 280,000 b/d. These shipments had largely been contracted one to two months earlier, Katona said.

The outlook will depend on whether China resumes larger diesel exports and how shipping costs to Europe evolve.

“If China starts flooding the Singapore and Southeast Asian markets, India will have no option other than to re-orient flows towards East Africa and Europe,” Katona said.

China’s planned return to diesel exports has already pushed down refining margins in Singapore to $64-65 per barrel, she added. If shipping costs to Europe remain high, Indian refiners may find it more profitable to sell their diesel in Asian markets instead.

Shokri said a possible recovery in Russian diesel production and exports could increase competition for Indian fuel, particularly in Europe, where shipments grew in September. The greater availability of Russian diesel could narrow price premiums and compress Indian refiners’ margins, he said.

The scale of the impact will depend on how much Russia can produce and export, given continuing refinery damage and export restrictions.

For India, the key variables are Chinese exports, Russian supply, regional diesel margins and freight rates. These factors will determine where Indian fuel can be sold most profitably as shifting trade flows and sanctions reshape the global diesel market.

(Edited by Tony Rai)

items.title: IonQ to buy cybersecurity firm Elisity in up to $1.3 billion deal
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Quantum computing company IonQ said on Monday it would buy cybersecurity firm Elisity in an all-stock deal valued at up to $1.3 billion, as it looks to expand its quantum security business.
items.body:
Quantum computing company IonQ (IONQ.N) said on Monday it would buy cybersecurity firm Elisity in an all-stock deal valued at up to $1.3 billion, as it looks to expand its quantum security business.
IonQ said the acquisition would provide it with expanded channels to bring its quantum offerings to both enterprise and government customers, helping them deal with current threats and prepare for attacks from future quantum computers.
Elisity, founded in 2019, has more than 100 customer deployments worldwide and has doubled its revenue and customer base year-over-year, IonQ said
The deal value includes up to $150 million in earn-outs tied to Elisity's performance, it added
The number of IonQ shares to be issued will be calculated at a price between $33.07 and $49.61 per share
"Q-Day is coming much faster than predicted," IonQ CEO Niccolo de Masi said, referring to the point when quantum computers could break widely used encryption
Elisity CEO James Winebrenner will continue to lead the acquired business after the deal closes
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approval
IonQ completed its acquisition of [USN:L6N3YR0UH TEXT:"chipmaker"] SkyWater Technology earlier this year to bring semiconductor manufacturing in-house and boost the development of its next-generation quantum processors

items.title: US immigration authorities raid home of Democratic Trump critic Ilhan Omar
items.author: Nolan Mccaskill, Andrew Goudsward, Doina Chiacu
items.creator: Nolan Mccaskill, Andrew Goudsward, Doina Chiacu
items.summary: Omar wrote on social media that the US government is being weaponized to target a political enemy of the president ahead of the midterm elections.
items.body:
US authorities conducted a predawn raid on Monday on the Washington, DC, home of Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump who has been the target of political insults by the Republican president, as part of an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said.
A person familiar with the investigation said it is related to alleged immigration fraud, and part of the probe concerns the Somali-born lawmaker's immigration paperwork filled out by her late father when she was a child.
Omar wrote on social media that the US government is being weaponized to target a political enemy of the president.
"For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns," Omar said. "This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced."
Other Democrats accused Trump and his administration of abuse of power. Omar, 44, is seeking a fifth two-year term in the US House of Representatives in the midterm elections on November 3.
In announcing the raid, a Justice Department spokesperson said: "Today in the Washington, DC area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation."
Homeland Security Investigations is part of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE.
'SOMETHING'S GONNA HAPPEN' Trump administration border czar Tom Homan told Fox Business Network that the Justice Department is leading the investigation with the Department of Homeland Security. Homan declined to address the specifics of an ongoing criminal investigation.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, a Trump appointee, said last month that "something's gonna happen" in the investigation into Omar's family's entry into the United States.
"If we can prove that you shouldn't have been here in the first place, we'll deport you," Mullin told conservative podcaster Benny Johnson at the time.
Monday's raid occurred a little more than three weeks before the midterms, with Trump's party seeking to retain control of Congress. Omar, a prominent progressive, represents a safe Democratic district. She won reelection in 2024 by a margin of 50 percentage points.
'DEEPLY DISTURBING' In a statement, US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries and other members of the party's leadership in the chamber said the raid was "deeply disturbing and raises serious questions" about the weaponization of the federal government against Trump's enemies.
Republicans have "relentlessly targeted" Omar, said Jeffries, joined by Representatives Katherine Clark and Pete Aguilar. Trump's "mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family," they added, and they vowed to "deliver full accountability" for a "rogue abuse of power."
Minnesota Democrats also condemned the raid.
"Americans see this for what it is," Minnesota Governor Tim Walz wrote on social media. "President Trump is abusing his power to go after political opponents weeks before an election."
Few Republican lawmakers publicly commented. One who did, Representative Nancy Mace, wrote online: "If the fraud is proven, she should be denaturalized and removed from this country. NO ONE is above the law."
Justice Department policy bars federal prosecutors and agents from timing any action to affect an election's outcome or benefit a candidate or party. It historically has avoided taking investigative steps against political candidates within about 60 days of an election.
George Washington University law professor Randall Eliason, a former US public corruption prosecutor, said the raid appears to be a break with past Justice Department practice of avoiding investigative steps likely to become public close to Election Day. But Eliason noted there is no way of enforcing the policy.
"The idea is to avoid even the appearance of any kind of interference by the Department of Justice with the political process," Eliason said. "It's not surprising that they wouldn't really care about violating this policy because they've shown they don't really care about politicizing the Justice Department in many other ways."
A person familiar with the investigation said the Justice Department consulted with its Public Integrity Section, a unit that has historically advised and approved investigations of members of Congress, and acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter prior to the search. The Trump administration has reduced the Public Integrity Section to about two lawyers and curtailed much of its authority.
INVESTIGATIONS OF TRUMP CRITICS The Justice Department during Trump's second term in office has investigated and brought charges against a range of Trump's perceived political enemies.
It has charged former FBI Director James Comey, New York state Attorney General Letitia James and Trump's former national security adviser turned critic John Bolton. It also has investigated Democratic lawmakers who urged the US military not to follow illegal orders, Democratic Senator Adam Schiff and Federal Reserve officials Jerome Powell and Lisa Cook.
The case against James and one of two brought against Comey were thrown out by a federal judge. Bolton pleaded guilty and is scheduled to be sentenced this month. Grand juries and federal judges have stymied several other probes.
'CREEPY OBSESSION' Omar has faced political insults from Trump, who has [USN:L1N45U12W TEXT:"cast"] the Somali American community as a threat to Minnesota in a burst of anti-Somali and anti-Muslim rhetoric. Omar has called Trump's focus on her an "unhealthy and creepy obsession."
Civil rights advocates have criticized Trump's rhetoric toward minorities and immigrants, including when he previously called Somalis "garbage."
Trump in February said Omar and Democratic Representative Rashida Tlaib, who also is Muslim, should be "institutionalized" and sent back to "where they came from." Both lawmakers criticized Trump during his State of the Union address as he touted his administration's immigration crackdown and enforcement actions.
Omar has said she and her family have faced death threats, which she attributes to "hateful political rhetoric," especially from Trump.
Last month, a Minnesota man who squirted vinegar on Omar [USN:L6N4591B6 TEXT:"was sentenced"] to 14 months in prison after pleading guilty to assaulting a federal official. Anthony James Kazmierczak admitted to attacking Omar because he disagreed with her progressive views.

items.title: Dólar opera en máximos 18 meses ante escalada Oriente Medio, mercado espera dato inflación EEUU
items.author: Laura Matthews
items.creator: Laura Matthews
items.summary: El dólar cotizó el lunes en un máximo de 18 meses, respaldado por la demanda de activos seguros ya que una escalada del conflicto en Oriente Medio mantuvo a los inversores cautos previo a datos de inflación en Estados Unidos que se publicarán más adelante esta semana.
items.body:
El dólar cotizó el lunes en un máximo de 18 meses, respaldado por la demanda de activos seguros ya que una escalada del conflicto en Oriente Medio mantuvo a los inversores cautos previo a datos de inflación en Estados Unidos que se publicarán más adelante esta semana.
* El índice dólar , que mide la evolución de la moneda estadounidense frente a otras seis divisas, subía un 0,4% a 102,58 unidades, un pico desde abril de 2025.
* Los precios del petróleo cotizaron con volatilidad después de que los hutíes de Yemen, respaldados por Irán, intensificaron sus ataques contra Arabia Saudita y de que dos petroleros fueron atacados durante el fin de semana.
* Los futuros del crudo Brent subieron 1,93 dólares, a 106,65 dólares por barril, cerca de máximos de dos semanas, ya que los ataques eclipsaron el anuncio del domingo del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, sobre un alto el fuego energético entre Ucrania y Rusia.
* El precio de los futuros sigue estando casi un 45% por encima del nivel que tenía antes de que comenzara la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán.
* La presidenta de la Reserva Federal de Cleveland, Beth Hammack, dijo el lunes que el banco central de Estados Unidos debería adoptar "con relativa rapidez" una postura de política monetaria restrictiva para controlar una inflación que, en su opinión, se ha generalizado y está empezando a influir en los planes de fijación de precios de las empresas.
* Los datos semanales del regulador de los mercados estadounidenses muestran que los inversionistas han ido aumentando sus posiciones alcistas en el dólar, que ascendieron a unos 36.000 millones de dólares en la semana que finalizó el 7 de octubre, frente a los apenas 8.400 millones de dólares de hace tres semanas , en gran parte a costa del euro.
* El reporte sobre la inflación al consumidor de Estados Unidos del miércoles, una de las últimas publicaciones económicas importantes antes de la reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal de este mes, podría ser clave para determinar la dirección a corto plazo del dólar.
* Los datos de la semana pasada mostraron que la confianza de los consumidores estadounidenses se deterioró aún más a principios de octubre, ya que el aumento del costo de la vida debido al conflicto en Oriente Medio empañó la visión que tienen los hogares de la economía.
* La Fed subió las tasas el mes pasado por primera vez desde 2023 para frenar la inflación, y los mercados siguen de cerca los datos económicos para evaluar si los responsables de política monetaria podrían volver a actuar.
* Los operadores descuentan una probabilidad del 78% de que la Fed mantenga las tasas sin cambios este mes, frente al 51% del mes anterior, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME.
* El euro caía un 0,4% a 1,1156 dólares, cerca de un piso de 17 meses, tras registrar la semana pasada su quinta semana consecutiva de pérdidas, debido a la inquietud de los inversionistas en torno a la salud fiscal de Francia de cara a las elecciones presidenciales de 2027.
* Frente al yen , el dólar subía un 0,2% a 158,57 yenes, en una sesión con escaso volumen de operaciones en Japón debido a un festivo, mientras que la libra caía un 0,2% a 1,3203 dólares.

GENEVA: Deep funding shortfalls are forcing the UN refugee agency to make painful cuts across its humanitarian operations worldwide, and there are limits to how much restructuring can offset shrinking donor support, its chief said on Monday (Oct 12).
UNHCR has secured only US$3 billion, or 35 per cent of the US$8.5 billion in funding it requires for 2026, High Commissioner Barham Salih told the agency's executive committee at a meeting in Geneva.
The shortfall follows aid cuts by countries including the United States under President Donald Trump at a time of record global displacement.
Funding for next year remains uncertain although the expected figure of around $2.68 billion could improve after a UNHCR donor pledging conference in December, Salih said.

UNHCR has launched one of its largest restructurings in the agency's history because of the budget squeeze, with Salih saying its workforce had been reduced since 2024 from 20,000 employees to just under 12,000.
"Protection has a floor. Below it, the system does not simply become smaller. The protection we can provide begins to fail," he said.
Salih cautioned that restructuring could not compensate indefinitely for lower funding, and that the funding crisis was already having tangible consequences for refugees and humanitarian partners.
"There is a difference between doing more with less and being asked to do the impossible," he said.

Related:

IN FOCUS: 'I cannot go back' - Myanmar refugees fear repatriation as country gets cosier with Malaysia, Thailand

Number of forcibly displaced people dips to 118 million: UN

JOB CUTS UNHCR is seeking to preserve frontline operations by cutting jobs at its Geneva headquarters and worldwide regional offices, with 88 per cent of staff remaining outside headquarters, Salih said.
About 95 per cent of the staff doing protection work, such as registering refugees and providing legal assistance, and helping refugees find longer-term solutions, such as returning home safely, have been retained in field locations, he said. 
He cited several examples of programmes under threat. 
In Chad, he said, insufficient funding risks disrupting specialised medical care and legal assistance for more than 50,000 survivors of conflict-related sexual violence who fled neighbouring Sudan. 
In Ethiopia, refugee registration had been suspended for tens of thousands of refugees from South Sudan and Eritrea, he said.
Colombia has raised concerns on behalf of Latin American countries that their region is being disproportionately impacted. 
The Americas, which include the US, Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean, face a budget reduction of 32 per cent in 2027 compared to this year, or about $485 million — the largest budget reduction of any region — while the number of forcibly displaced and stateless people in the Americas is projected to increase by 4 per cent to about 24.5 million people in 2027, Salih said.

Source: Reuters/ia

items.title: ＥＵのＨＶ輸入上限枠、中国ＥＶ各社に打撃　欧州現地生産加速へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［上海／北京　１２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［上海／北京　１２日　ロイター］ - 中国が欧州連合（ＥＵ）向けのハイブリッド車（ＨＶ）輸出を抑えることに同意した。国内販売の伸びが鈍る中、中国の電気自動車（ＥＶ）メーカーにとって新たな打撃になる。

中国商務省は１２日、この取り決めで輸出は今後も増やせるとし、中国には他のどの輸入元に割り当てられる枠よりも小さくない数量枠が保証されると表明した。

中国自動車各社は、ＥＵの中国製ＥＶに課す関税の対象外であるＨＶの輸出を増やしてきた。中国税関のデータによると、２０２６年上半期のＥＵ向けＨＶ輸出額は７５億ドルと、前年同期（２５億ドル）の３倍だった。

ジェフリーズによると、上海汽車集団（ＳＡＩＣ）、比亜迪（ＢＹＤ）、奇瑞汽車の３社が、ＥＵで販売される中国製ＨＶの９割超（台数ベース）を占める。３社の欧州販売では、半分以上がＨＶとなっている。

シュミット・オートモーティブ・リサーチによると、欧州ＥＶ市場での中国ブランドのシェアは２６年第２・四半期に過去最高の１５％となった。２４年第１・四半期は９．５％だった。ＰＨＥＶ市場でも中国製のシェアは４分の１を超え、２４年初めのわずか１．７％から急拡大した。

＜現地生産加速へ＞

仏ルノーのフランソワ・プロボ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は１２日、中国製ＨＶの輸入急増は欧州にとって持続可能ではないと述べた。一方で、今回の合意は貿易戦争よりは望ましいとし、通商関係を「賢明に」管理する必要があると指摘した。

投資家はおおむね、今回の合意を貿易摩擦の緩和と受け止め、中国製ＨＶへの関税が当面は見送られる兆しとみている。

シティのアナリストは、実施ルール、数量上限、最低価格などは、今後さらなる協議が必要だが、とりあえずリスクが緩和したと指摘した。

中国の自動車業界に詳しいコンサルタントのマイケル・ダン氏は「中国が合意を守るのか、それとも抜け道や一時的な関税免除を見つけるのか、見ていきたい」と述べた。

アナリストらは、数量枠の制度が始まる前に輸出を前倒しする動きが出る可能性があるが、合意は最終的に、中国の自動車メーカーによる欧州での現地生産を加速させる可能性があるとみる。

上海のコンサルティング会社オートモビリティの創業者、ビル・ルッソ氏は「これで、中国の自動車メーカーが欧州で生産する動機は強まるだろう」と述べた。

仏ルノーのフランソワ・プロボ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は１２日、中国製ＨＶの輸入急増は欧州にとって持続可能ではないと述べた。一方で、今回の合意は貿易戦争よりは望ましいとし、通商関係を「賢明に」管理する必要があると指摘した。

投資家はおおむね、今回の合意を貿易摩擦の緩和と受け止め、中国製ＨＶへの関税が当面は見送られる兆しとみている。

シティのアナリストは、実施ルール、数量上限、最低価格などは、今後さらなる協議が必要だが、とりあえずリスクが緩和したと指摘した。

中国の自動車業界に詳しいコンサルタントのマイケル・ダン氏は「中国が合意を守るのか、それとも抜け道や一時的な関税免除を見つけるのか、見ていきたい」と述べた。

アナリストらは、数量枠の制度が始まる前に輸出を前倒しする動きが出る可能性があるが、合意は最終的に、中国の自動車メーカーによる欧州での現地生産を加速させる可能性があるとみる。

上海のコンサルティング会社オートモビリティの創業者、ビル・ルッソ氏は「これで、中国の自動車メーカーが欧州で生産する動機は強まるだろう」と述べた。

Surfing hotspots around the world are more vulnerable to climate change, says new study

The research analysed 57 surf breaks across eight countries to arrive at its findings. Each of the sites selected is incorporated into a World Surfing Reserve.

Purvi Rajpuria

12 October, 2026 04:43 pm IST

New Delhi: Many of the most prominent surf breaks across the world are vulnerable to climate change, even as the degree and type of vulnerability differ widely, a recent study found. 

The study, titled ‘ Globally significant surf breaks are vulnerable to climate change ’, was co-authored by Dan R Reineman of California State University Channel Islands, along with researchers from Save The Waves Coalition and World Surfing Reserves . 

The research analysed 57 surf breaks across eight countries to arrive at its findings. Each of the sites selected is incorporated into a World Surfing Reserve (WSR)—“a status applied for by local stakeholders and designated by an international non-profit organization based on each site’s cultural, historical, and environmental significance for surfing,” the study explains.

Show Full Article

These surf breaks, the research found, are vulnerable to climate change, due to changing tide levels, hardened shorelines caused by manmade structures, and shifting sands. Surf breaks rated at most risk include Croyde beach in north Devon, UK, and Oriente Salvaje in El Salvador. 

What are surf breaks?
Dan Reineman, a co-author of the study, pointed to the several factors that come together to form a surf break. “Surf breaks are incredibly unique oceanographic phenomena – a confluence of all these factors that fit together just right to make the wave happen – and so those processes are really sensitive,” he said .

Some of these factors include swell direction, tide, and intricate combinations of sea-floor shape. Climate change, global warming, and changing rainfall patterns can affect any of these factors, hampering the delicate balance of surf breaks and thus destroying the wave. 

Significantly, the study found that coastlines that were more natural and less populated by manmade structures could adapt better to the changes caused by climate change. These coastlines were able to adapt by shifting inland and relocating sediments. Construction of features such as sea walls, jetties and groynes made the beaches and waves less resilient, Reineman said .

Also read: Mamdani has a new target. Subscriptions that make cancellations difficult

Affects local economy at large
Climate change-related vulnerability matters not only to surfers, but also to the local people who depend on the multi-billion-dollar surf economy that exists in these sites. 

Adam Hall, a co-founder of the North Devon WSR, was one of the local surfers who contributed to the study. Explaining the significance of surfing to the local economy, he said , “Surfers will come throughout the year. They fill up the pubs, restaurants and car parks when the swells are good in January, February and March, where if you go to any other tourist destination that doesn’t have surf, they’re dead on their knees.”

Many of these sites often have little else in terms of local economy. 

Local surfers also played a key role in guiding the research. Trent Hodges, a co-author of the study and a senior programmes manager at Save the Waves Coalition, said , “We learned directly from the local surfers how they are seeing their waves change. It’s a canary in the coalmine too – when a wave changes, that often means the beach is changing, and everybody enjoys the beach.”

The study also hypothesises that similar risks could affect other surf breaks, not included in the present research, and encourages other local people and organisations to assess their vulnerability. 

(Edited by Ratan Priya)

FAST

Oct 12 : Norway's data protection authority has fined Microsoft's adtech unit Xandr 92 million crowns ($9.61 million) for unlawfully relaying Grindr users' sensitive data to thousands of advertisers, it said on Monday.
Xandr relayed data revealing the sexual orientation of users of Grindr, a dating app for LGBTQIA+ people, to companies in automated ad auctions from July 2018 to April 2020.
It is the biggest fine the Norwegian authority has issued, and targets the advertising middlemen rather than the app itself. The regulator said companies that traded in people's data could not pass the blame to others.
The data protection authority fined Grindr 65 million crowns over the same breaches in 2021.

The fine was based on Xandr's revenue, not Microsoft's, which did not own the unit at the time. Xandr has three weeks to appeal.
Xandr said it assumed Grindr had obtained users' consent and never checked, the data protection authority said. It rejected that argument and ruled Xandr shared legal responsibility with Grindr. 
Microsoft said the privacy of users was a top priority.
"This investigation and decision focused on conduct that predates Microsoft's acquisition of Xandr, and in that time the interpretation and application of legal standards and practices has continued to evolve. We are reviewing the decision and assessing our options," it said.
The case began with a 2020 complaint by the Norwegian Consumer Council, whose research exposed how apps shared user data, and Austrian data privacy organisation noyb, which called the decision "a valuable precedent".  
($1 = 9.5704 Norwegian crowns)

items.title: Crudo sube tras los ataques a Arabia Saudita, lo que eclipsa el acuerdo de Trump sobre diésel
items.author: Shadia Nasralla
items.creator: Shadia Nasralla
items.summary: Los precios del petróleo subieron casi 2 dólares por barril el lunes, ya que los ataques contra Arabia Saudita pesaron más que la perspectiva de un aumento de la oferta, a pesar de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, celebró las nuevas exportaciones rusas de diésel y el alto el fuego entre Rusia y Ucrania en materia de objetivos energéticos.
items.body:
Los precios del petróleo subieron casi 2 dólares por barril el lunes, ya que los ataques contra Arabia Saudita pesaron más que la perspectiva de un aumento de la oferta, a pesar de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, celebró las nuevas exportaciones rusas de diésel y el alto el fuego entre Rusia y Ucrania en materia de objetivos energéticos.
*Los futuros del crudo Brent cerraron con una subida de 1,93 dólares, o un 1,8 %, hasta los 106,65 dólares por barril, su nivel más alto desde el 15 de septiembre. El crudo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) de Estados Unidos cerró en 93,74 dólares por barril, con una subida de 1,89 dólares, o un 2 %.
*Los hutíes, alineados con Irán, reivindicaron la autoría de un ataque perpetrado el sábado contra el aeropuerto internacional de Riad, en el que murieron 13 personas y más de 300 resultaron heridas. El domingo se produjeron nuevos ataques, lo que intensificó un conflicto que podría obstaculizar aún más el suministro de crudo procedente de uno de los mayores productores del mundo.
*"El impactante ataque con misiles de los hutíes contra el aeropuerto de Riad, en Arabia Saudita, provocará, obviamente, una escalada de las represalias contra los hutíes en Yemen", afirmó el inversor y analista Louis Navellier en una nota. "En estos momentos, las refinerías de Arabia Saudita están en funcionamiento, pero cinco de ellas se cerraron temporalmente cuando se interrumpió un oleoducto hacia el mar Rojo tras los ataques con misiles".
*Este mes se han registrado más ataques contra petroleros que navegaban por el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que amenaza con frenar la recuperación de las exportaciones de crudo de Oriente Medio observada en septiembre.
*Un petrolero fue alcanzado por un dron en las proximidades de Sohar, en Omán, mientras que otro sufrió daños al transitar por el estrecho de Ormuz, según informó la Agencia de Operaciones de Comercio Marítimo del Reino Unido.
*"La sensación de cierta normalidad en las exportaciones desde el estrecho de Ormuz se hizo añicos la semana pasada. Los nuevos ataques de los hutíes contra Arabia Saudita se sumaron a ello y contribuyeron a la subida de los precios", afirmó Bjarne Schieldrop, analista de materias primas de SEB.
*"Cada vez habrá que tomar decisiones más difíciles sobre qué defender: la infraestructura petrolera, las instalaciones militares, los palacios reales, los aeropuertos civiles u otros".
*Goldman Sachs, en una nota, elevó su previsión del precio del Brent para diciembre de 85 a 90 dólares por barril, estimando una prima de riesgo de algo más de 20 dólares por barril.
*Los precios del WTI, añadieron, probablemente se mantendrían bajos frente al Brent debido a los elevados costos de transporte entre Estados Unidos y Europa, y se situarían en una media de 81 dólares en diciembre de 2026 y de 73 dólares en 2027.
*En el Golfo de México, las grandes empresas energéticas Shell (SHEL.L) , Chevron (CVX.N) y BP intentaban reubicar a su personal y restablecer la producción en sus plataformas después de que el huracán Isaías tocara tierra la madrugada del sábado.
