items.title: Nasdaq falls ahead of earnings, economic data while oil rallies
items.author: Sinead Carew, Ragini Mathur
items.creator: Sinead Carew, Ragini Mathur
items.summary: The technology-heavy Nasdaq composite closed lower on Monday as oil prices jumped nearly $2 a barrel after attacks on a Saudi airport, and investors waited for banks to kick off the third-quarter earnings season and for economic data this week.
items.body:
The technology-heavy Nasdaq composite closed lower on Monday as oil prices jumped nearly $2 a barrel after attacks on a Saudi airport, and investors waited for banks to kick off the third-quarter earnings season and for economic data this week.
The S&P 500 ended the session barely lower while the Dow advanced.
Oil futures rallied after deadly [USN:L1N45X01E TEXT:"strikes on Riyadh's international airport"] over the weekend. The attacks overshadowed the prospect of increased supplies after US President [USN:L1N45X021 TEXT:"Donald Trump"] hailed fresh Russian diesel exports and talked about a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire on energy targets.
In coming days, US investors will focus on corporate earnings, with major US banks including Goldman Sachs (GS.N) , Citigroup (C.N) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) reporting early on Tuesday. Analysts were expecting S&P 500 earnings to surge 30.6% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES data.
Also due out this week are September readings for US consumer and producer inflation as well as retail sales data. While the US Treasury market was closed on Monday for Columbus Day, stock investors have been wary of bond yields' recent advance to [USN:L8N45T173 TEXT:"24-year highs"] as elevated energy prices have stoked inflation concerns.
"Looking out further in the week, we have some big economic reports," said Tim Ghriskey, senior portfolio strategist at Ingalls & Snyder in New York. He said investors were also cautious due to a lack of direction from bonds.
"We're also waiting on earnings and that's significant. The four large banks reporting on Tuesday can have a big impact," he said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 195.60 points, or 0.38%, to 51,850.55, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 4.30 points, or 0.06%, to 7,807.24 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 120.27 points, or 0.44%, to 27,245.90.
Trading volume was relatively light with 12.67 billion shares changing hands on US exchanges compared with the 20-day moving average of 17.62 billion.
"There's a lot to be wary of," said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth in Fairfield, Connecticut, pointing to upcoming data and earnings along with rising oil prices.
"You're walking down a train line and you don't know, because it's dark, if a train is coming and so, you know, you're just being real careful," he said.
With oil prices rising, energy (.SPNY) outperformed among the S&P 500's 11 major industry sectors with a 1.5% advance. The defensive consumer staples sector (.SPLRCS) rose more than 1% along with the S&P 500 communication services index (.SPLRCL) , which was boosted by a more than 3% gain in heavyweight Meta (META.O) .
Technology (.SPLRCT) , down 0.9%, and consumer discretionary (.SPLRCD) , off 0.7%, were the biggest sector laggards. Technology's weakness was most pronounced among chip stocks with the Philadelphia semiconductor index (.SOX) finishing down 2.7% after hitting a three-week low.
In consumer discretionary, Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG.N) shares fell 3.8% after Starbucks (SBUX.O) said [USN:L4N45Y0TM TEXT:"it was not buying"] the burrito chain. Starbucks shares closed up 1.7%.
Microsoft (MSFT.O) finished up 1.1% with its market capitalization climbing above $4 trillion for the first time in a year after it [USN:L6N45V11Z TEXT:"announced plans for major deployment"] of its own AI chips.
Salesforce (CRM.N) shares added 2% after BofA Global Research upgraded the stock to "buy" from "underperform." Also eBay (EBAY.O) rose 2% after Morgan Stanley added the stock to its top-pick list.
Meanwhile, Cleveland Federal Reserve President [USN:S0N44V02D TEXT:"Beth Hammack"] said the US central bank should move "relatively quickly" to a more restrictive monetary policy stance to fight inflation, which she feels has become more broad-based and is starting to influence firms' price-setting plans.
Traders were pricing in an almost 22% chance the US Federal Reserve will hike interest rates this month, according to CME's FedWatch tool, up from 17.7% on Friday.
Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.09-to-1 ratio on the NYSE where there were 149 new highs and 272 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 1,888 stocks rose and 3,008 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.59-to-1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 10 new 52-week highs and five new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 51 new highs and 318 new lows.

items.title: ノーベル経済学賞、米大教授2人に　経済安定化の研究
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ストックホルム　１２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ストックホルム　１２日　ロイター］ - スウェーデン王立科学アカデミーは１２日、２０２６年のノーベル経済学賞を米スタンフォード大学のロバート・ホール教授（８３）と米コロンビア大学のマイケル・ウッドフォード教授（７０）に授与すると発表した。授賞理由は「マクロ経済の安定化に関するミクロ経済学的基盤」。

両氏は、効果的な安定化政策を実行する能力を向上させる新たなボトムアップ型の経済モデルを開発した。これにより、経済に打撃を与える変動の激しさを緩和できる、適切なタイミングでの財政・金融政策の実施が可能となり、世界の中央銀行や財務省で活用されている。

経済学賞選考委員会のジョン・ハスラー委員長は声明で「両氏の功績は、現在世界中の各中央銀行や政府によって使われているモデルに安定した理論的基盤を提供した」と指摘。「両氏のモデルによって、エネルギー危機や家計消費の急変動など、経済へのショックにより適切に対処できるようになった」と述べた。

両氏の重要な洞察の一つは、経済の仕組みを上から捉えるトップダウン型の理論に頼るのではなく、家計や企業がミクロのレベルで下す無数の決定を考慮して初めて経済を安定させられるという点だ。

ウッドフォード氏は会見で「当局は、経済の安定化を、経済の中にいる人々がそれをどう理解しているかとは関係なく、誰かがレバーを引いて経済を操作するだけの作業と見なすべきではない」と語った。

ウッドフォード氏によると、中銀が高騰するインフレへの対応に苦しんだ１９７０年代の石油危機とは違い、２０００年代後半の世界金融危機では、新たな枠組みが伝統的な金融政策手段を補う上で役に立った。

「すぐに追加利下げできることだけに頼るのではなく、金利政策が今後どうなりそうかをより明確に表明することが、０９年以降の政策対応の重要な部分を占めた」と述べた。

両氏の研究は、金融政策の先行きを示す、いわゆる「フォワードガイダンス」のほかにも、需要が変化しても価格の変化が遅れる「粘着的な」インフレ、「需給ギャップ（アウトプットギャップ）」といった現在使われている概念を広めた。

items.title: Most Americans oppose betting on elections, government events, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
items.author: Chris Prentice, Jason Lange
items.creator: Chris Prentice, Jason Lange
items.summary: Most Americans oppose using prediction markets to bet on US elections and other government actions, according to a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll that suggests the booming markets may lack broad public support as policymakers debate how to regulate them.
items.body:
Most Americans oppose using prediction markets to bet on US elections and other government actions, according to a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll that suggests the booming markets may lack broad public support as policymakers debate how to regulate them.
The [USN:L4N42Y0WQ TEXT:"rapidly growing prediction market industry"] led by Polymarket and Kalshi allows people to bet on a raft of events, including US elections, government policy moves and sports games, raising concerns among policymakers that the platforms are opening up new avenues for [USN:L6N44E0TQ TEXT:"insider trading"] and manipulation.
The companies say they have [USN:L4N42H1L3 TEXT:"extensive controls"] to guard against misconduct, that their markets are often better at forecasting outcomes than traditional polls, and that they [USN:L6N44L0X4 TEXT:"offer unique ways to hedge"] a range of esoteric real-world risks.
Yet a bipartisan majority of Americans is opposed to using prediction markets to bet on US elections , military actions and government policy announcements or decisions, according to the Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted September 30 through October 5.
Some 69% of Democrats and 61% of Republicans said they opposed using prediction markets to bet on election results.
Sixty-five percent of Americans opposed prediction market betting on US military actions and 63% opposed betting on government policy announcements or decisions, suggesting broad bipartisan discomfort with wagering on government affairs. Only 8% and 9%, respectively, supported such bets.
The results shed more light on popular attitudes toward the nascent industry, which is marketing heavily on social media and TV even as it faces pushback from states and from Democratic lawmakers who argue the markets are unethical, socially corrosive and could undermine national security.
"Everyone should make their own decisions about their lives," said Ronna Schmoker, 72, a Democrat from a Dallas suburb who participated in the poll. "But like anything, you have to have guardrails."
A Polymarket spokesperson said Americans are bombarded with misinformation from various sources, and that prediction markets help provide unbiased, accurate information.
"It’s why more than 90% of visits to Polymarket are to view markets, not to trade," the spokesperson said. "Recognition of the public value of prediction markets is growing, but they’re still brand new to most, and it’s going to take some time for the public to learn more and see the real value."
NATIONAL SECURITY AND ELECTION FEARS HAVE STOKED DEBATE Some policymakers worry that prediction markets, which offer thousands of ways to wager on the US midterms, [USN:L6N41V1AT TEXT:"could undermine faith in"] the integrity of US democracy and enable government insiders to broadcast confidential information via their trades.
Reuters reported [USN:L6N44E0TQ TEXT:"in August"] that more than 150 accounts on Polymarket International, the company's overseas market which bars US users, may have traded on inside military information, while Kalshi [USN:L1N41514R TEXT:"has suspended candidates"] for betting on their own races.
Kalshi banned former Republican Representative George Santos, who agreed to pay $35,000 [USN:L6N43X19K TEXT:"to resolve government allegations"] of manipulative trading after he bet via Kalshi on whether he would attend the State of the Union address. Santos did not admit to the allegations and said through his attorney that he never intended to deceive anyone.
Ninety-three percent of Democrats and 89% of Republicans said it was inappropriate for members of Congress or their staff to bet on political events, while 6% and 8%, respectively, said it was appropriate.
Polymarket and Kalshi say they work closely with the authorities and routinely refer suspicious accounts, and have introduced various restrictions to mitigate misconduct.
Kalshi says it does not allow trading on military operations and bars political candidates from wagering on their own races. The Senate in April barred senators, staff and other officers from using prediction markets, and [USN:L4N4051K3 TEXT:"several Democratic lawmakers have introduced bills"] to restrict the industry.
"We see prediction markets everywhere, but don't mistake seeing millions of dollars in advertisements as a sign of growing support," said Democratic Senator Jeff Merkley of Oregon. "Folks are rightfully concerned."
The Reuters/Ipsos poll suggests many Americans are generally uneasy about increasingly commoditizing real-world events. Even betting on professional sports, a far more established activity, was opposed by 43% of respondents, while 29% supported it.
"I just don't think it's good for a society to bet on whether things will turn out a certain way," said Michael Clark, a 48-year-old conservative who lives outside Dallas and participated in the poll.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS SUPPORTED INDUSTRY GROWTH The administration of President Donald Trump, whose son Donald Trump Jr. has business ties to Kalshi and Polymarket, is pursuing federal regulations for the industry, a move states are fighting. Legal experts expect that dispute to reach the Supreme Court.
At issue is whether prediction markets facilitate trading in financial instruments or gambling, which is regulated by the states. State regulators say they are facilitating gambling and should be subject to more stringent state laws, while Trump's Commodity Futures Trading Commission has asserted jurisdiction, arguing the contracts are a type of financial product it regulates.
"By that rationale, MGM (Resorts) owns dozens of financial markets," said Glenn Rishton, a 76-year-old Republican poll respondent in Gulfport, Mississippi, referring to the casino company. "It's effectively gambling."
Three-quarters of Americans agreed, with only 8% saying using prediction markets to wager on the outcome of real-world events is not a form of gambling.
A spokesperson for the Coalition for Prediction Markets said its research found that Republican and Democratic voters alike prefer a federal regulatory framework over a patchwork of state rules.
The Reuters/Ipsos poll, which was conducted online and nationwide, surveyed 4,506 US adults and had a margin of error of about two percentage points.
"Prediction markets should have the same level of regulations as gambling," said Janessa Manning, 48, a Democrat in Detroit. "Even though they pretend they aren’t gambling, they are."

items.title: Citi seeks rapid resolution of its US regulatory burdens
items.author: Tatiana Bautzer, Nupur Anand
items.creator: Tatiana Bautzer, Nupur Anand
items.summary: Citigroup is seeking to rapidly resolve its efforts to address regulatory demands that have long dogged the third-largest US bank, in order to fully re-focus on growth, according to two people familiar with the matter.
items.body:
Citigroup (C.N) is seeking to rapidly resolve its efforts to address [USN:L6N3YV14X TEXT:"regulatory demands"] that have long dogged the third-largest US bank, in order to fully re-focus on growth, according to two people familiar with the matter.
The demands have lingered since 2020, leading to costly fines and distractions for Citi.
As recently as the summer, Citi was targeting submitting paperwork to regulators before the end of the year, or during the first quarter, one of the people told Reuters.
The bank has been aiming to present a comprehensive audit to the Federal Reserve and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, so it will not hit any delays in approval, the person said. It will then wind down part of its remediation structure, the two sources said.
This would finally set the bank on a path to have consent orders lifted. The orders cover the regulatory [USN:L6N3YV14X TEXT:"demands to fix "]risk management, data governance and other problems.
Investors and analysts are laser focused on when Citi might shake off its regulatory burden, which could free up resources, boost the stock and become a key achievement for Chief Executive Jane Fraser.
Fraser has said Citi is about 90% done with the regulatory work required under the orders.
SPEEDING UP Wells Fargo analyst Mike Mayo said an exit "would be seen as a validation of their restructuring process, and Citigroup shares may then attract a larger group of investors".
Earlier this year, Reuters reported that the bank had hoped to finish the job by the end of 2026.
While Citi has never acknowledged an official timeline, the person familiar with the matter said that it is under pressure to achieve this as soon as possible, but ran into a brief audit-related delay over the summer.
Citi did not comment on any motivation for getting out of the consent orders as soon as possible, but said such a decision rested with regulators.
"The way Citi is run today is fundamentally different from where we started our Transformation, and we are committed to ensuring the changes we have been making to strengthen our risk and control environment are sustainable," a Citi spokesman said.
"As we have said consistently, we will not speculate about the lifting of the consent orders because that remains solely at our regulators’ discretion," the spokesman added.
AREAS OF PROMISE Citi's regulatory [USN:L6N3XN1GA TEXT:"distractions"] have come at a time when rivals have taken advantage of the government's lighter-touch banking policies, including over supervision and rules, analysts say.
Filings show the bank spent $3.3 billion on "transformation" work last year. It is set to [USN:L1N45R0GT TEXT:"report its earnings on Tuesday"].
In a research report, Bank of America analyst Ebrahim Poonawala said Citi's wealth division "shows the greatest room for improvement" among its five core franchises, for which it needs to accelerate growth of investment assets, and tilt revenues toward fee income and away from spread income.
The division still has the lowest return of all five businesses, at 12.6% in the first half of the year, with a long term goal of 20%.
The two people familiar with the matter said the wealth management and retail businesses could benefit from increased scale, with one potential solution being to add branches or acquire a wealth manager.
While such moves to expand are not formally prohibited under the consent orders, they are more closely scrutinized by regulators, reinforcing the need to quickly address their demands.
"It is tougher to focus on any relevant growth before you fix the problems," said Tim Long, a former deputy comptroller at the OCC. "It makes sense for the bank to try to get the orders finalized in this (Trump) administration and avoid potential change of regulators and a different approach."
FAVORABLE POLICIES Any potential acquisition would force Citi to consider both regulators' and investors' appetite, especially after speculation of an imminent deal was [USN:L4N40F1AJ TEXT:"badly received "][USN:L4N40F1AJ TEXT:"by the market"] earlier this year.
Fraser later told investors on an earnings call: "We are only interested in and focused on organic growth. Period. End of story".
The Trump administration , now nearing the midpoint of its term, has so far been broadly favorable for banks, despite the president attacking some firms including [USN:L4N3YN1QS TEXT:"JPMorgan"] and [USN:S0N3OG012 TEXT:"Bank of America"].
Trump has on the other hand praised Citi in a social media post for its investment banking growth.
Financial regulators under Trump have addressed several of the industry's longstanding gripes, including trimming barriers to mergers as part of the administration's overall bid to ease regulation.
Some industry executives say they are wary that a future Democratic administration could reconsider these policies.
DATA TRACING Citi's road to fixing past errors has been long and bumpy.
It traces back to a botched $900 million transfer to Revlon creditors, which triggered a 2020 demand by the Federal Reserve and OCC to remediate longstanding risk management and data governance problems. It was fined $400 million and the bank agreed to fix the identified issues.
Four years later, the OCC fined it again for a delay in addressing data and other problems related to the original consent orders and requested in an amendment that Citi come up with a plan showing the resources it would allocate to address the issues. The OCC lifted that amendment in December 2025 [USN:L4N3XO1DA TEXT:"but the original consent order was outstanding"].
One of the people who spoke to Reuters said that the bank had carefully checked remediation work to be shown to the regulator, with one internal audit in the summer rejecting a version presented on data tracing – specifically, the ability to track the origin of aggregated accounts.
Making sure the internal audits are rigorous will be key to streamlining the process and avoid extensive checks on Citi's work, the person said.
The lifting of the consent orders would require sign-off from the Fed and OCC. The Fed declined to comment for this article. The OCC did not respond to a request for comment.

items.title: Hall, Woodford win Nobel prize for work on how to stabilise economies
items.author: Simon Johnson, Johan Ahlander
items.creator: Simon Johnson, Johan Ahlander
items.summary: US academics Robert Hall and Michael Woodford won the 2026 Nobel economics prize on Monday for decades of work developing ground-up models currently used by central banks and finance ministries across the world to stabilise economies.
items.body:
US academics Robert Hall and Michael Woodford won the 2026 Nobel economics prize on Monday for decades of work developing ground-up models currently used by central banks and finance ministries across the world to stabilise economies.
"With them, we are better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy, such as energy crises or sudden changes in how much households consume," John Hassler, Chair of the Committee for the Prize in Economic Sciences, said in a statement.
Woodford and Hall are frequently name-checked by the world's [USN:L6N45A0IG TEXT:"top central banks"] which, after a 2022 inflation surge in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, are currently grappling with the energy shock triggered by the Iran war .
One of the laureates' key insights is that economies could only be kept on an even keel by taking into account the millions of decisions made at a micro-level by households and businesses, rather than by using top-down theories of how economies work.
"Authorities shouldn't view stabilization of the economy as an exercise that is simply conducted by people pulling levers to control the economy independently of what people in the economy understand about this," Columbia University's Woodford, 70, told a news conference.
In contrast to the oil shocks of the 1970s, when central banks struggled to combat sky-high inflation, Woodford said the new framework was useful during the global financial crisis of the late-2000s to bolster traditional tools of monetary policy.
"Making more explicit statements about the likely future path of interest rate policy, as opposed to relying on simply being able to cut interest rates further immediately, that was an important part of the policy response in the years from 2009 onward," he said.
Beyond so-called "forward guidance" on the future path of monetary policy, the work of Woodford - and Hall, 83, at Stanford University – promoted other concepts used today such as the idea of "sticky" inflation when price changes lag changes in demand.
Another is the "output gap", a measure of demand pressure building up in an economy and how efficiently resources are being used, with the goal of stabilisation policy being to steer that gap towards zero.
CORE CENTRAL BANK CONCEPTS Hall has served as adviser to the US Treasury Department, the Justice Department and the Federal Reserve Board.
His insight in a 1978 paper that household decisions on consumption are a perfect indicator of their expectations was used by Woodford in a model on how consumption is determined.
Hall called the prize "a wonderful surprise" in a statement.
"I've spent my career trying to understand how the economy works," he said. "When I thought I had a new idea, the next step was to find out whether it was actually new, whether it was right, and whether it mattered."
Woodford also showed that central banks can stimulate or suppress economic activity by adjusting interest rates, rather than just by the amount of money in circulation.
Such concepts remain core to [USN:L1N40L06U TEXT:"central banking today"]. Forward guidance became especially important after the 2008 financial crisis, when rates were near zero or even negative and standard monetary policy seemed to be out of ammunition.
Now, however, some are questioning how relevant it is given the amount of uncertainty in the global economy – with new US Federal Reserve Chair [USN:L6N43T122 TEXT:"Kevin Warsh"] a notable sceptic.
The economics prize, formally known as the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, is the final award to be given out this year and is worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million).
First awarded in 1969, it is not one of the original five awards created in the 1895 will of industrialist and dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel, but was established by Sweden's central bank.
The majority of previous laureates have been from the United States. Only three women have ever won, most recently Claudia Goldin in 2023 for work on how gender has affected pay and employment over time in the United States.
[USN:L2N3VU08K TEXT:"Last year's winners"], Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt, won for work on "creative destruction" and how new technology and production methods can boost growth and living standards.
The Nobel prizes for [USN:L1N45R0AK TEXT:"medicine"], [USN:L1N45S0E6 TEXT:"physics"], [USN:L1N45T09K TEXT:"chemistry"], [USN:L1N45U0CQ TEXT:"literature"] and [USN:L8N45V0JG TEXT:"peace"] were announced last week.
($1 = 10.0028 Swedish crowns)

items.title: Kyiv says Russia hits energy targets despite Trump ceasefire announcement
items.author: Daniel Flynn, Pavel Polityuk
items.creator: Daniel Flynn, Pavel Polityuk
items.summary: Russia hit at least six energy targets during deadly airstrikes across Ukraine, showing it had no interest in an energy ceasefire announced by US President Donald Trump, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday.
items.body:
Russia hit at least six energy targets during deadly airstrikes across Ukraine, showing it had no interest in an energy ceasefire announced by US President Donald Trump, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday.
Under pressure over high energy prices ahead of US midterm elections next month, Trump blindsided Kyiv and its European allies over the weekend by declaring that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to hit each other's energy systems.
"It is increasingly evident that Russia is unwilling to accept an energy ceasefire proposed by the United States and intends to continue its terrorist air attacks against our people and communities," Zelenskiy said on X.
"This is what happens when Russia sees the prospect of higher revenues for its war machine."
In earlier comments by video link to a conference in Poland, Zelenskiy identified two of the targets as a gas facility and a petrol station, both hit by Russian drones.
Trump announced the purported energy ceasefire days after unveiling a [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"deal to buy diesel from Russia"], which Zelenskiy has criticised as a reversal of years of Western policy aimed at isolating Russia's economy.
Trump, for his part, has called on Ukrainians to unseat Zelenskiy in an election, an unusually severe exchange in a relationship between the two leaders that has been strained since Trump returned to power in 2025.
Russian President Vladimir Putin's point man for oil, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak, [USN:L1N45Y0MF TEXT:"said"] Moscow would be able to return diesel exports to levels above those Trump outlined under the diesel deal.
Trump [USN:L1N45Y0QE TEXT:"defended"] the deal as US lawmakers from both major parties complained that it appeared to violate US law. The president's envoys [USN:L1N45Y0OS TEXT:"told Ukrainian officials"] last week that the deal sought to draw Russia back to talks on ending the war, three people familiar with the meeting told Reuters.
Trump's weekend announcement on an energy ceasefire was the second time within a few weeks that Trump had issued such a declaration without confirmation from the two warring sides.
Ukraine's European allies on Monday voiced scepticism of any such agreement, spoke in support of Kyiv and [USN:L8N45T1J0 TEXT:"approved the largest set of EU sanctions"] since Russia's 2022 invasion.
"Russia will only negotiate seriously under pressure, which is why we are sticking to our sanctions against Russia," German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin.
'WE DO NOT WANT A CEASEFIRE,' KREMLIN SAYS Kyiv has increasingly targeted Russian oil refineries and logistics with long-range strikes, its answer to more than four-and-a-half years of relentless Russian attacks on its cities, including persistent campaigns to knock out Ukraine's power and heat in successive winters.
Zelenskiy said Ukraine had carried out no attacks on Russian refineries overnight and was willing to agree an energy ceasefire, but said it was [USN:L8N45Y12U TEXT:""increasingly clear""] Russia would not abide by it. He also said elections, suspended during wartime, could be held if Moscow agreed to a full ceasefire for 60 days.
Russia said talks [USN:R4N45F02J TEXT:"were proceeding"] about a possible energy ceasefire, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said further information would be revealed in due course. But he rejected Zelenskiy's proposal for a full 60-day truce.
"In the Kremlin, both President (Vladimir) Putin and officials at other levels have repeatedly stated that we do not want a ceasefire," said Peskov. "We want long-term peace and are prepared to do everything possible to achieve it."
BODY AMONG WRECKAGE In Kyiv, a new Russian strike on a high-rise apartment block killed two people and injured at least nine, while attacks in other regions killed at least six people, officials said.
New strikes also targeted Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-biggest city in the northeast.
Ukraine's Emergency Services said 11 people had been injured in evening attacks, including one strike which triggered the collapse of an entrance to an apartment building.
Overnight attacks killed at least three people in Kharkiv and further strikes in the morning wounded at least 22.
Three people were killed near Kramatorsk one of Ukraine's "fortress cities" in eastern Donetsk region that Russian forces have set their sights on in their slow advance westward.
In Kharkiv, Nataliia Minka said she had just made it to a shelter when a missile struck nearby. She and her child had seen what they believed to be a missile hitting a power station.
"Ten minutes had passed since they promised they wouldn’t target energy facilities," she said.
"It’s so hard to describe how a child was lying there, already covered up, and the father was running around her, crying and screaming," she added.
Russia began its latest strike campaign on Ukraine's grid two weeks ago, already causing daily, hours-long power cuts in Kyiv, affecting the capital's water and sewage systems and twice bringing its underground trains to an abrupt halt.
To maintain pressure on Moscow, European Union foreign ministers on Monday added 1,569 new names to their sanctions list of banned individuals and businesses, billed as the largest single package to date.
Trump has increasingly blamed Kyiv's attacks on Russian refineries for surging global costs for fuel, especially diesel, which has hit record U.S prices since he launched his military campaign against Iran. On Saturday, he said Zelenskiy had [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:""better damn well stop""] attacking Russian refineries.
items.raw_description: Russia hit at least six energy targets during deadly airstrikes across Ukraine, showing it had no interest in an energy ceasefire announced by US President Donald Trump, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday.

items.title: Philippine lower house approves bill restricting minors' social media access
items.author: Nestor Corrales, Mikhail Flores
items.creator: Nestor Corrales, Mikhail Flores
items.summary: The Philippines on Monday moved a step closer to restricting social media use among minors after its lower house of Congress approved a measure banning access to platforms for children under 13.
items.body:
The Philippines on Monday moved a step closer to restricting social media use among minors after its lower house of Congress approved a measure banning access to platforms for children under 13.
The Philippines is the latest country, from Greece and Portugal to Australia, [USN:L6N41Z08Z TEXT:"Malaysia "]and [USN:L4N40E0HB TEXT:"Indonesia,"] to try to curb [USN:L8N42Q0MC TEXT:"social media use by minors,"] as concern grows over its effects on child health and safety.
The House of Representatives voted overwhelmingly in favour of limiting minors' access to social media platforms, following on from the Senate's recent endorsement of a similar bill.
The two chambers will now be required to reconcile their bills then submit a final draft for presidential approval.
The progress of the legislation comes after three school shootings since June in the Philippines that reignited [USN:L6N44G0IZ TEXT:"debate"] over children accessing social media and online content.
A 16-year-old last month [USN:L4N45A0KH TEXT:"shot dead"] at least two fellow students before turning the gun on himself, while in August, a student [USN:L6N44F03Q TEXT:"live-streamed"] himself shooting and killing a classmate before taking his own life.
Gun violence at schools was previously rare in the Philippines.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr said on Sunday he had been studying the bill passed by the Senate and that a blanket ban on social media could cause children to hide their online activities, leaving them vulnerable to grooming and abuse.
The Senate's version is stricter than the draft approved by the lower house and bans anyone under 18 from creating social media accounts.
TikTok, YouTube owner Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , and Meta Platforms (META.O) , the owner of Facebook and Instagram, did not immediately respond to separate requests for comment on the Philippines house passing the bill.
Neighbouring Malaysia in June began barring under-16s from registering accounts on social media platforms, which are required to conduct age verification against government-issued records.
Malaysia has given social platforms until January 2027 to implement the measure.
Indonesia issued a regulation in March requiring social media firms with platforms it deems high risk to deactivate accounts belonging to children under 16, which have so far included X, Instagram and video game platform Roblox.
As of last week, TikTok has deactivated around 9 million accounts belonging to children under 16 in Indonesia, while Meta has blocked 85,000 Instagram accounts and 99,000 Facebook accounts.

LONDON, Oct 12 : Artificial Intelligence needs urgent global regulation with independent evaluators able to vet new developments, the president of Microsoft said, warning that AI currently faces fewer safety requirements than milk.  
In an interview with the BBC published on Monday, Brad Smith said a set of global safety rules needed to be in place, requiring a "victim" to be informed if their system is breached by a rogue AI agent and an "emergency brake" available.
He said there should also be a legal requirement for companies to write "incident reports". 
"We know how to do this for other products," Smith said. "We should build on that knowledge and think about how to apply it to AI."

"Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI. Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection."
Tech companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI have started disclosing rogue or undesired behaviour by AI agents as part of a global debate about the fast-advancing technology that has included researchers' warnings of an eventual existential threat to humanity.
Some companies have called for AI development to slow down, but that has sparked a debate as to whether executives have ulterior motives such as setting rules that preserve the lead of their firms, pre-empting a broader government backlash, or simply slowing breakneck spending.
Microsoft's Smith said the one country that was well-placed to lead the way on regulation of AI was Britain, due to the AI Security Institute which was launched under former prime minister, Rishi Sunak. 
Smith said officials in Washington viewed London very differently to how they viewed Brussels, which regulates AI based on the level of risk via its AI Act.
Britain's institute receives pre-deployment access under voluntary agreements with the major AI models, allowing it to assess their capabilities and risks. 
AI Minister Kanishka Narayan has told Reuters that Britain would consider regulating advanced models if the current system proved insufficient.

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 12 : The dollar held at an 18-month high on Monday, supported by safe-haven demand as attacks escalated in the Middle East over the weekend, keeping investors cautious ahead of key US inflation data later this week.
The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against six others, was up 0.37 per cent at 102.58, highest since April 2025.
Oil prices were volatile after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis stepped up strikes on Saudi Arabia, and two tankers were attacked over the weekend. 
Brent crude futures rose 2.3 per cent to $107.17 a barrel, nearing a two-week high. The attacks overshadowed Sunday's announcement from US President Donald Trump about an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia that seemed imperiled from the get-go, as Kyiv accused Russia of violating the ceasefire overnight.

Brent crude is still nearly 45 per cent above where it was before the US-Israeli war with Iran started.
Meanwhile, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said on Monday that the Federal Reserve should move "relatively quickly" to a restrictive policy to control inflation she sees as more broad based.
Investors have been increasing bullish positions on the dollar, which as of the week ended October 7 came to about $36 billion, up from $8.4 billion three weeks ago, largely at the expense of the euro.
"We aren’t convinced this latest bout of risk aversion will translate into sustained dollar strength," said Joel Kruger, market strategist at LMAX Group in London, citing cooling economic data, inflation pressures moderating, and much of the Fed's expected rate hikes already priced into the market. "We see limited scope for additional dollar upside." 
SPOTLIGHT MOVES TO US INFLATION DATA 
Wednesday's US consumer inflation report, one of the last major economic releases before the Fed's policy meeting this month, could be critical in determining the near-term direction of the dollar. 
US consumer sentiment deteriorated further in early October, as the rising cost of living because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy.
The Fed raised rates last month for the first time since 2023 to rein in inflation. Traders are pricing in a 78 per cent chance of the Fed standing pat this month, up from 51 per cent a month earlier, the CME FedWatch tool showed.
"The real focus is on the CPI number this week - it is likely to be running hot," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex in New York. He added that a rate hike before an election is so uncommon that "the bar is kind of high" for the Fed to act.
Investors have grown worried about the sharp selloffs in bond markets that have driven borrowing costs across the globe to multi-decade highs. 
The euro fell 0.4 per cent to $1.1156, near a 17-month low, after clocking a fifth straight week of losses last week, driven by investor angst around France's fiscal health before the 2027 presidential election.
The spread between French 10-year yields and safer German yields traded at 140 basis points. Last week it neared 160 bps, the most since 2012.
"There's been no improvement and no real clear guidance as to what's going to make things better in the short term," said Dan Tobon, head of G10 FX strategy at Citi in New York. "What's the reason to buy European debt, to buy euro here? It's hard to find one, and so we just kind of keep drifting off."
The US dollar rose 0.2 per cent to 158.66 yen, while the pound slipped 0.2 per cent at $1.3203.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Saudi capital's airport to remain shut this week as airlines cancel services
items.author: Gianluca Lo Nostro, Menna Alaaeldin, Joanna Plucinska
items.creator: Gianluca Lo Nostro, Menna Alaaeldin, Joanna Plucinska
items.summary: Authorities have extended the closure of Riyadh's international airport until Saturday and airlines scrapped flights after continuing attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis emptied the skies over Saudi Arabia's capital.
items.body:
Authorities have extended the closure of Riyadh's international airport until Saturday and airlines scrapped flights after [USN:L6N45Y0OR TEXT:"continuing attacks"] by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis emptied the skies over Saudi Arabia's capital.
Operations at King Khalid International Airport, Saudi Arabia's second-busiest airport after Jeddah, were suspended to "allow for the completion of procedures to ensure the safety and operational readiness of the airport's facilities", the Saudi civil aviation authority said in a statement.
Late on Monday, the Houthis said they had attacked the airport with a ballistic missile, shortly after Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the group towards Riyadh.
The Houthis also said in a statement that they targeted an airbase in Khamis Mushait in the kingdom's southwest with a drone. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation.
A Notice to Airmen issued on Monday showed that the King Khalid International Airport will stay closed until 2100 GMT on October 17.
The airport has been shut since an attack on Saturday that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. On Sunday, another attack killed one person and injured nearly a dozen others.
The attacks marked one of the most significant disruptions to Saudi aviation in years, adding to pressures on an industry already grappling with conflict across the Middle East and with higher jet fuel prices that are eating into profits.
They have also raised worries over civil aviation becoming a target in armed conflict.
"This level of sustained intense attack on civil aviation is unprecedented," said Mark Zee, founder of OPSGROUP, a membership-based organization that provides aviation safety advice.
"I think this requires us to rethink how we view the current risk picture, and tread very carefully," he said.
Air traffic tracker Flightradar24 showed planes avoiding the city on Monday, though jets were crossing Saudi airspace and landing at top hub Jeddah on the country's west coast.
Cancellations across all Saudi airports reached 46.4%, aviation analytics firm Cirium said.
CRISIS OVERSHADOWS SAUDI BUSINESS OUTLOOK The disruption has forced airlines across Europe and Asia [USN:L4N45Y0QL TEXT:"to suspend services"], while the Federal Aviation Administration advised US carriers on Sunday to [USN:L1N45X078 TEXT:"exercise caution"] when flying to or over Saudi Arabia. EU aviation body EASA widened a Saudi [USN:L6N45V0KQ TEXT:"airspace warning"] on Friday, citing missile and drone attacks.
"The impact goes beyond Saudi Arabia to the wider region and to its global connections," said aviation analyst John Strickland.
OPSGROUP advised airlines to avoid the southern aviation corridor over the Middle East altogether, and take a route from Europe to Asia over central Asia.
That adds "extensive distance" for some routes and "closes off options for getting into Dubai, Abu Dhabi for most western carriers," Zee said.
Lufthansa Group (LHAG.DE) [USN:L6N45U10R TEXT:"has cancelled"] all flights to Riyadh until October 16, while Air France-KLM (AIRF.PA) has extended a suspension to and from Riyadh until the end of the month. Abu Dhabi's Etihad Airways also extended cancellations.
Delta Air Lines (DAL.N) said it was delaying planned services from Atlanta to Riyadh, initially due to start on October 23, until March 2027.
The escalation with the Houthis has raised concerns over the broader economic impact. Saudi Arabia's real GDP is [USN:L1N45M0WE TEXT:"projected to contract"] by 3.6% this year, reflecting a combination of factors including lower oil activity.
The attacks have put [USN:L8N45W01K TEXT:"events scheduled"] in Riyadh this month under pressure, including the kingdom's flagship investment conference and the WPC Energy Congress, where several top oil executives [USN:L6N45Y0GT TEXT:"were dropped from"] the programme.

items.title: L'aéroport de Ryad restera fermé cette semaine après deux attaques meurtrières
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Les autorités saoudiennes ont prolongé lundi pour le reste de la semaine la fermeture de l'aéroport international de Ryad, capitale de l'Arabie saoudite, après que ce dernier a été la cible de deux attaques meurtrières dont une samedi, revendiquée par les Houthis qui a fait 13 morts et plus de 300 blessés.
items.body:
Les autorités saoudiennes ont prolongé lundi pour le reste de la semaine la fermeture de l'aéroport international de Ryad, capitale de l'Arabie saoudite, après que ce dernier a été la cible de deux attaques meurtrières dont une samedi, revendiquée par les [USN:L8N45W036 TEXT:"Houthis"] qui a fait 13 morts et plus de 300 blessés.
Cette attaque a entraîné la décision de fermer l'aéroport dimanche, jour où, selon les termes de la coalition dirigée par l'Arabie saoudite au Yémen, un [USN:L8N45X06H TEXT:""projectile non identifié""] lancé contre le terminal 4 a fait un mort et onze blessés.
L'aéroport international Roi Khaled sera fermé jusqu'au 17 octobre à 21h00 (GMT), selon un message publié par les agences gouvernementales de contrôle de la navigation aérienne.
Les opérations à l'aéroport, le deuxième du pays en termes de fréquentation après celui de Djeddah, ont été suspendues afin de "permettre l'achèvement des procédures visant à garantir la sécurité et la disponibilité opérationnelle des installations de l'aéroport", déclare dans un communiqué l'autorité saoudienne de l'aviation civile.
Lundi soir, les Houthis ont déclaré avoir attaqué l'aéroport avec un missile balistique, peu après que Ryad eut rapporté avoir intercepté et détruit un tir lancé par le groupe.
Les autorités saoudiennes avaient auparavant émis une alerte contre une "menace hostile" potentielle dans la capitale, selon un message consulté par Reuters.
Le mouvement aligné sur l'Iran a également revendiqué une attaque de drone sur une base aérienne de Khamis Mushait, ville du sud-ouest du royaume. L'Arabie saoudite n'a pas confirmé dans l'immédiat cette offensive.
La compagnie aérienne allemande Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) a annulé tous ses vols à destination de Riyad jusqu'au 16 octobre, tandis qu’Air France-KLM (AIRF.PA) a prolongé jusqu'à la fin du mois la suspension de ses liaisons vers et depuis la capitale saoudienne.
La compagnie Etihad Airways, basée à Abou Dhabi, a également prolongé ses annulations de vols vers l'Arabie saoudite, affectant une vingtaine de vols à destination de Ryad, Djeddah et Dammam lundi et mardi.
Ces attaques perturbent le congrès énergétique du World Petroleum Council qui a commencé dimanche à Ryad, avec notamment la décision de la directrice générale de BP (BP.L) Meg O'Neill d'annuler sa venue.
L'Arabie saoudite a renforcé son engagement militaire au Yémen ces dernières semaines, menant des frappes contre les Houthis et soutenant une contre-offensive des forces gouvernementales après que le groupe s'est emparé le mois dernier de secteurs stratégiques le long de la côte de la mer Rouge.
Les Houthis, les rebelles proches de l'Iran qui contrôlent une bonne partie du Yémen dont la capitale Sanaa, ont dit que toute nouvelle action militaire saoudienne au Yémen entraînerait une riposte de plus grande ampleur, ajoutant que ses actions seraient guidées par le principe de réciprocité.
Les Houthis résistent depuis 2014 à une coalition mise sur pied par l'Arabie saoudite, en s'appuyant sur un arsenal de drones et missiles balistiques constitué avec l'aide de Téhéran.
Les combats font rage depuis des semaines sur plusieurs fronts au Yémen, alors que la guerre civile, globalement latente depuis 2022, a regagné en intensité avec le conflit entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran.
Fin septembre, le ministère des Finances saoudien a déclaré que le produit intérieur brut (PIB) du royaume devrait se contracter de 3,6% cette année, en raison notamment des perturbations provoquées sur son activité pétrolière par la guerre entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran et par le conflit contre les Houthis.

items.body:
テスラ、9月の中国製ＥＶ販売5％増に加速　欧州で回復続く
10/12 15:59 配信

2026年4月14日、上海のテスラ・ギガファクトリーで撮影。 REUTERS/Go Nakamura

[北京 ９日 ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラの９月の中国製ＥＶ販売台数は前年同月比５％増加し、８月の３．６％増から伸びが加速した。欧州での販売回復が続いた。

中国乗用車協会（ＣＰＣＡ）が９日発表したデータによると、上海工場で生産されたセダン「モデル３」とＳＵＶ（スポーツ多目的車）「モデルＹ」の納車台数は、欧州、アジア太平洋地域、カナダへの輸出を含め９万５３６６台と、前年同月の９万０８１２台から増加し、１１カ月連続の前年比プラスとなった。 

• ９月の新車登録台数は欧州の複数の市場で増加し、同地域での販売回復が続いた。

• ＣＰＣＡのデータに基づくロイターの算出によると、上海工場で生産されたＥＶの第３・四半期販売台数は前年同期比１３．７％増加した。一方、世界全体の納車台数は、過去最高を記録した２０２５年第３・四半期と比べ２．１％減少した。

• テスラの第３・四半期の世界納車台数は市場予想を上回り、通年で３年ぶりに増加に転じる見通しだ。

• 世界最大の自動車市場である中国では激しい競争が続いており、テスラは１０月末まで、一部の「モデルＹ」で７０００元（１０４４ドル）、全ての「モデル３」で５０００元を最終支払額から割り引く販促を実施している。

items.summary: ［上海　１１日　ロイター］ - 米アップルに部品を供給する中国の立訊精密工業（ラックスシェア・プレシジョン・インダス...
items.body:
アップル供給元の中国立訊精密、米で特許侵害調査　影響軽微と説明
10/12 15:56 配信

北京で6月に開催された中国国際サプライチェーン博覧会（CISCE）」の立訊精密のブース　REUTERS/Florence Lo

［上海　１１日　ロイター］ - 米アップルに部品を供給する中国の立訊精密工業（ラックスシェア・プレシジョン・インダストリー）は１０日、米国で新たに始まった特許侵害調査による悪影響は軽微との見通しを示した。積極的に対応を進め、株主の利益を守ると説明した。

１０日夜に公表された取引所への届け出に基づく詳細は以下の通り。

＊米国際貿易委員会（ＩＴＣ）は１０月９日、米バイコーによる特許侵害の申し立てを受け、同社と子会社の東莞立訊技術を対象に、米関税法３３７条に基づく調査を開始。

＊ＩＴＣの調査は初期段階。対象は垂直給電システムと関連部品、それらを搭載したコンピューティングシステムで、ＩＴＣはまだ実質的な判断を示していない。

＊対象製品はデータセンター向けの電源モジュールや電力供給ソリューションに使われるもので、まだ量産は開始していない。このため、調査が事業運営や短期的な業績に重大な悪影響を及ぼす可能性は低い。

＊同社は対象の特許と製品の検証を既に開始し、技術、法務、事業の各チームを組織して対応を準備している。

＊顧客やサプライチェーン（供給網）のパートナーとの連携を強化し、会社と株主の利益を積極的に守る。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [北京 １２日 ロイター] - 中国の国内自動車販売は９月、１２カ月連続で減少した。一方、自動車メーカーが国内市場の低...
items.body:
中国の国内自動車販売、12カ月連続減少　輸出は好調維持
10/12 15:52 配信

写真は中国・上海の港の輸出ターミナルに並ぶ新車。７月撮影。China Daily提供写真。REUTERS

[北京 １２日 ロイター] - 中国の国内自動車販売は９月、１２カ月連続で減少した。一方、自動車メーカーが国内市場の低迷による影響を和らげようと海外市場に目を向ける中、輸出は引き続き成長を支える主要な要因となった。

中国乗用車協会（ＣＰＣＡ）が１２日発表したデータによると、９月の国内乗用車販売は前年同月比２８．１％減の１６３万台だった。減少率は８月の２３．７％から拡大した。

一方、９月の自動車輸出は前年同月比７３．２％増の９２万３０００台だった。８月は７７．５％増だった。

• 電気自動車（ＥＶ）とプラグインハイブリッド車（ＰＨＶ）の国内販売は前年同月比１６．７％減の１０８万台。８月の１０．１％減から減少率が拡大した。一方、輸出の伸び率は８月の１５４．７％から１６３．５％に加速した。

• ＣＰＣＡの崔東樹秘書長（事務局長）は新エネルギー車の輸出ではＥＶが大きな割合を占めるため、ＰＨＶの輸出が制限されても、新エネルギー車全体の輸出に大きな影響が及ぶ可能性は低いと述べた。

• 欧州連合（ＥＵ）のシェフチョビッチ欧州委員（通商担当）は９日、中国とＥＵが、中国からＥＵへのハイブリッド車輸出を４年間で半減させる可能性のある合意に達したと述べた。ただ、輸出数量の上限や、その枠を超える輸出に適用される条件は依然として不明だ。

• 国内販売の減少は、経済全体の弱さを反映している。個人消費の低迷と不動産不況の長期化が需要を圧迫している。

• 規制当局は成長重視から安全性と価値重視へと軸足を移しており、十分な検証を経ない拙速な新車投入を抑える規則を提案している。

NEW DELHI, Oct 12 : Oil prices slipped on Monday on expectations of more Russian supplies after US President Donald Trump said Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on each other's energy facilities following a US diesel-supply deal with Moscow.
Brent crude futures fell 11 cents, or 0.11 per cent, to $104.61 a barrel by 0627 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $91.36 a barrel, down 49 cents, or 0.53 per cent. Both benchmarks were down more than 1 per cent earlier in the session.
ICE gasoil futures fell 3 per cent to $1,436 per metric ton after President Trump said on Friday that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons (2.25 million barrels) of diesel to US and global markets.
Russia would supply another 500,000 tons in November and a further 1 million tons "immediately thereafter", Trump added. The daily diesel consumption globally is forecast at close to 29 million barrels, according to the International Energy Agency.

Trump also unexpectedly announced on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to an energy ceasefire, but Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was still waiting to see details of the energy ceasefire while Russia did not comment.
The announcements eased some of the immediate supply pressure, Tim Waterer, KCM Trade chief analyst, said.
"Questions remain over the validity and longevity of any such ceasefire, and without clearer evidence that it will actually hold, the extent of the pullback is likely to stay limited," he added.
IEA's Executive Director Fatih Birol said on Sunday that all members should assess whether additional diesel releases are necessary and that countries which have not yet fully delivered pledged volumes accelerate their remaining releases prioritising diesel.
CRUDE SUPPORTED BY MIDDLE EAST CONFLICT
However, the Middle East conflict continued to support Brent crude at above $100 a barrel.
The Houthis claimed responsibility for a Saturday strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, while Saudi authorities reported that people were injured in a new attack on the airport on Sunday.
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war with Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.
In addition, more attacks on tankers sailing through the Strait of Hormuz have been reported so far this month, threatening to dampen a recovery in Middle East crude exports seen in September.
A tanker was struck by a drone in the vicinity of Sohar anchorage, Oman, while another was damaged by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported over the weekend.
Goldman Sachs raised its Brent crude price forecast for December to $90 a barrel, up from $85 previously, its analysts led by Daan Struyven said in a note.
"We maintain our base case that continued adaptation of Mideast supply will eventually reduce crude oil prices, while potential renewed escalation still poses significant net upside risk," the analysts said, estimating a risk premium of just over $20 a barrel.
"We forecast WTI prices, which are unusually low vs Brent because of high US-Europe shipping costs, to average $81 in December 2026 and $73 in 2027," they added.
In the Gulf of Mexico, energy majors Shell, Chevron and BP were seeking to redeploy personnel and restore production at their platforms after Hurricane Isaias made landfall early on Saturday.

Source: Reuters

items.title: 中国、先端技術の監督強化へ　ＡＩ制御・バブル防止で新指針
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［北京　９日　ロイター］ - 中国は９日、先端技術分野の推進に向けた政策指針を発表した。中国は、米国との対立を背景に、...
items.body:
中国、先端技術の監督強化へ　ＡＩ制御・バブル防止で新指針
10/12 15:01 配信

上海で開催された世界人工知能会議で2025年7月撮影　REUTERS/Go Nakamura

［北京　９日　ロイター］ - 中国は９日、先端技術分野の推進に向けた政策指針を発表した。中国は、米国との対立を背景に、ハイテク製造業や戦略産業への支援を強化しているが、新興分野への盲目的な投資や過剰な拡大に警告を発し、監督体制を強化する方針を示した。人工知能（ＡＩ）を「安全で信頼でき、制御可能」な状態に維持することを目指す。

習近平国家主席は２０２３年に「新質生産力（新たな質の生産力）」という概念を打ち出し、科学研究や技術的な突破口の開拓、中国全土の製造拠点における産業高度化を重視してきた。

新華社によると、中国共産党と国務院（内閣に相当）が発表した指針は「新質生産力の発展は、質の高い発展を推進するための本質的な要請であり、重要な重点事項である」としている。

指針によると、中国はＡＩ理論や中核技術の突破口を目指すとともに、計算能力（コンピューティングパワー）、アルゴリズム、データの供給を強化し、産業用ＡＩ応用の国家実証拠点を設置する。一方でＡＩが「安全で信頼でき、制御可能」であり続けるよう、技術監視、リスク警告、緊急対応の各体制を整備するよう求めた。

「ＡＩプラス」構想を全面的に実施し、ＡＩを活用して従来型産業を高度化させ、コネクテッド新エネルギー車（ＮＥＶ）、ＡＩ搭載のスマートフォンやパソコン、人型ロボットなどのスマート製品の普及を加速させる。

中核技術における「独自かつ破壊的」なイノベーションを強化し、国家主導の「新型挙国体制」を活用して象徴的な製品の開発・展開を加速するとした。

同時に、当局は実体経済を優先し、バブルや産業の空洞化、盲目的な投資、ハイテク分野への「群がるような」殺到を防止すべきと指摘した。

「新質生産力の発展を名目とした違法または不適切な政策の乱用を厳格に禁止する」とし、盲目的な投資によって重大な損失をもたらした担当当局者に責任を負わせると述べた。

また、安全性を確保しつつ、民間用ドローンや空飛ぶタクシー、小型航空機および関連サービスを中心とする「低空経済」の健全で秩序ある発展も求めた。

items.title: Model blitz at Paris motor show as Europe-China rivalry heats up
items.author: Nick Carey, Giulio Piovaccari
items.creator: Nick Carey, Giulio Piovaccari
items.summary: Europe's car industry fought back against rising Chinese competition at the Paris car show on Monday with a wave of new model launches and fresh support from Brussels, even as Chinese automakers expanded their push into the region.
items.body:
Europe's car industry fought back against rising Chinese competition at the Paris car show on Monday with a wave of new model launches and fresh support from Brussels, even as Chinese automakers expanded their push into the region.
The show opened days after the European Union announced a deal with China to curb imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles into the bloc, with a [USN:B5N44302K TEXT:"cap"] of 350,000 a year, according to a European Commission official. While details of the arrangement have yet to be finalised, it was broadly welcomed by European manufacturers, though some said more support would be needed.
Stellantis (STLAM.MI) CEO Antonio Filosa said the deal was a "good milestone", but that the Fiat maker was also seeking help with high energy costs from the Italian government and wanted Brussels to move more quickly on carbon emissions rules.
The flood of Chinese hybrid imports into the EU is "not sustainable", Renault (RENA.PA) CEO Francois Provost said, describing the agreement as "better than a trade war".
Zhao Fei, president of Chinese automaker Changan (000625.SZ) . said he was "not that concerned" by the deal, which he viewed as a precursor to "Made in Europe" local content rules that could be dealt with by setting up production in the region.
Around [USN:L1N45S104 TEXT:"20 Chinese brands"], including BYD (002594.SZ) and Chery (9973.HK) , are attending the show, double their presence in 2024 as they seek growth overseas amid intense competition and weaker demand at home.
Chinese brands have gained share rapidly in Europe over the last three years, while [USN:L4N45Y073 TEXT:"Chinese exports of hybrids"] to the EU's 27-member states tripled to $7.5 billion in the first half of this year, according to Chinese customs.
The EU-China deal could hit BYD, Chery and state-owned SAIC's (600104.SS) MG brand hardest as between them they accounted for 90% of Chinese brand hybrid sales in the EU in the first eight months of 2026, Jefferies analysts said on Sunday.
BYD said the deal amounted to short-term pressure but that it remained committed to Europe.
Underscoring the challenges facing European manufacturers, Volkswagen said on Monday its deliveries fell [USN:L6N45Y0A9 TEXT:"14.3%"] in the third quarter, the steepest quarterly drop in four years, dragged down by a further decline in demand in its top market, China. Deliveries also fell in North America and Western Europe.
As part of its efforts to regain market share in Europe, Stellantis is launching six new models across its European brands at the show and unveiling nine concept cars.
On Sunday evening, CEO Filosa hailed "the reinvention of a European icon" as he unveiled an affordable retro electric version of [USN:L6N3SF0GW TEXT:"Citroen's 2CV"].
The company is also adopting faster Chinese-style development cycles, Chief Technology Officer Ned Curic said, outlining plans to build small EVs in Italy using a platform being developed with China's Leapmotor.
Renault's head of growth, Fabrice Cambolive, [USN:S8N42Q0EZ TEXT:"said"] on Monday the carmaker could increase EV production in France by at least 50% over the next 12 months.
'IF THEY DROP EXPORTS ... THEY DIE' Like other Western motor shows, Paris had been in decline until Chinese automakers began turning up in force four years ago.
Alongside BYD and Chery, this year's show features newer Chinese entrants including Aito, while state-owned Changan is launching its Nevo and Avatr brands in Europe.
Chinese automakers also used the event to outline further European expansion plans. Changan's Zhao [USN:FWN45V1M3 TEXT:"said the company"] was in talks with manufacturers about producing vehicles in Europe and hoped to build its first European-made car in early 2027.
BYD is [USN:L6N45Y0J7 TEXT:"studying the possibility"] of building a factory in France, Executive Vice President Stella Li told broadcaster BFM TV.
The EU imposed tariffs on Chinese-made fully electric vehicles in October 2024. Brussels is also working on "Made in Europe" rules requiring minimum local content levels for EVs to access large parts of the bloc's market.
Agreement between France and Germany on the provisions is "imminent", French President Emmanuel Macron said at the show.
Chinese automakers have sought European production bases ahead of the proposed rules, often in partnership with established manufacturers.
In July, China's [USN:L1N43P0D0 TEXT:"Geely Auto"] (0175.HK) said it would produce electric SUVs at a Ford Motor (F.N) factory in Spain.
Separately, India's Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis [USN:L4N45Y0L2 TEXT:"said on Monday"] they had expanded their partnership to include technology and product development, with plans to build vehicles in India for more than 50 global markets.
Car sales in China, the world's largest auto market, fell 20% in the first half of 2026, increasing pressure on manufacturers to expand overseas.
As the US market is effectively closed to China's auto industry, Europe has become its top export priority.
"If they drop exports in Europe they die because they can't make the money elsewhere," said Francois Roudier, secretary general of the International Organisation of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers.

items.title: Ｓ＆Ｐ、英格付け「ＡＡ」に据え置き　エネ価格高騰でも経済堅調
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [９日 ロイター] - 格付け会社Ｓ＆Ｐは９日、英国のソブリン格付けを「ＡＡ／Ａ─１プラス」に据え置き、見通しは「安定...
items.body:
Ｓ＆Ｐ、英格付け「ＡＡ」に据え置き　エネ価格高騰でも経済堅調
10/12 14:15 配信

2026年6月9日、英ロンドンで撮影。 REUTERS/Chris J. Ratcliffe

[９日 ロイター] - 格付け会社Ｓ＆Ｐは９日、英国のソブリン格付けを「ＡＡ／Ａ─１プラス」に据え置き、見通しは「安定的」とした。中東紛争に起因するエネルギー価格高騰にもかかわらず、英経済が底堅さを示していることを理由に挙げた。

第２・四半期の英国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）は前期比０．５％増加し、２０２６年上半期の同国経済は主要７カ国（Ｇ７）の中で最も高い成長率を記録した。

Ｓ＆Ｐは声明で「中東紛争にもかかわらず、個人消費とサービス業、特に宿泊・飲食業や専門サービス業が比較的底堅く推移し、第２・四半期の成長を支えた」と指摘した。

２６年上半期の経済成長が予想を上回ったことを踏まえ、Ｓ＆Ｐは２６年の英成長率見通しを１．３％に引き上げ、２７─２９年は平均１．４％の成長を見込むとした。

バーナム首相率いる新政権は、財政圧力の高まりと借り入れコストの上昇に直面する中、経済政策の見直しを目指している。

Ｓ＆Ｐは、議会で過半数議席を握っていることがバーナム氏に政策課題を推進する裁量を与えているものの、生計費高騰という大きなショックへの対応が必要となっており、歳出計画は歳入の制約や、過度に高い税負担による成長鈍化リスクとのバランスを取る必要があるとした。

items.title: ＡＩ投資で世界成長率約3％維持、アジアに大きな恩恵＝ＩＭＦ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Andrea Shalal

[バンコク １２日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のゲオルギエワ専務理事は１２日、...
items.body:
ＡＩ投資で世界成長率約3％維持、アジアに大きな恩恵＝ＩＭＦ
10/12 13:59 配信

写真は国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のゲオルギエワ専務理事。バンコクで１２日撮影。REUTERS/Athit Perawongmetha

Andrea Shalal

[バンコク １２日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のゲオルギエワ専務理事は１２日、人工知能（ＡＩ）インフラへの旺盛な投資によって世界経済の成長率が３％前後に維持されており、タイなどハードウエアを供給する多くのアジア諸国が大きな恩恵を受けているという認識を示した。

タイの首都バンコクでこの日開幕したＩＭＦ・世界銀行年次総会で、ＡＩ投資ブームは既に「需要ショック、投資ショック」をもたらしていると指摘。アジア先進国の経済成長率を０．５─１．０％ポイント、アジア新興国の成長率を０．２─０．８％ポイント押し上げる可能性があると述べた。

「エネルギー供給ショックが足かせとなっているにもかかわらず、世界経済が３％前後の成長を維持しているのは、こうした投資の加速によるものだ」と語った。

ＩＭＦは７月、２０２６年の世界経済成長率を３％と予測した。１３日に最新の見通しを公表する。

＜ＡＩがもたらす大きな影響＞

ゲオルギエワ氏は、ＡＩを「ゆっくりと押し寄せる津波」に例え、雇用や成長、教育に大きな影響を及ぼすと指摘。労働から資本への移行が見込まれることから、政府が課税を通じて税収を確保する仕組みにも大きな影響が及ぶとの見方を示した。 

ＩＭＦの推計では、ＡＩによって、時間の経過とともに雇用の４０％が能力強化、あるいは質や価値の低下、消失につながる可能性があるという。初期の調査では、米国の雇用の１０％で既にＡＩスキルが求められていることが示された。定型的な反復作業を伴う仕事が減る一方、賃金水準が比較的低い建設とデータセンターの２分野では、低賃金の仕事が増えているという。   

ゲオルギエワ氏は「ＡＩは変革をもたらす技術だ。われわれの働き方や暮らし方を根本から変える」と述べ、自身も今ではＡＩアシスタントから毎日、予定について３０秒間の案内を受けていると紹介した。

ＡＩのサプライチェーン（供給網）では米国、中国、インドが最も重要な生産国だが、必要なインフラを構築する企業の多くはアジアにあると指摘。今年の年次総会の開催国タイにも言及した。

＜新卒採用への影響＞

雇用問題を総裁任期中の中心課題に掲げる世界銀行のバンガ総裁は、世銀が大規模言語モデルに依存しない「スモールＡＩ」の活用に重点を置き、新興国市場の農家、医療制度、教育関係者などに大きな生産性向上をもたらすことを目指していると述べた。 

同じイベントに登壇したシンガポールのシャンムガラトナム大統領は、ＡＩによって新卒者の就職機会が減っている問題に各国政府が対応すべきだと述べた。

「われわれが早急に取り組まなければならない問題がある。就業の最初の段階、つまり卒業後に初めて就く仕事への需要が今減っていることだ」と語った。

ＡＩが途上国と先進国の間で、成長と雇用創出を巡る「新たな格差」を生むことにも警戒すべきだと指摘した。

Hurricane Simon weakens to Category 3 as rains flood Mexico's Pacific coast

MANZANILLO, Mexico: Hurricane Simon weakened to a Category 3 storm on Sunday (Oct 11) as it moved parallel to Mexico's Pacific coast, bringing strong winds and heavy rain that flooded homes.
The storm, packing maximum sustained winds of 205kmh, was located about 175km west-northwest of the port city of Manzanillo at 6pm, the US National Hurricane Center (NHC) said.
"Additional weakening is forecast but Simon is still expected to be a strong hurricane as it passes near the coast of west-central Mexico tonight," the forecaster's advisory said.
Simon was moving northwest at 7kmh and was expected to move farther offshore on Monday before turning back toward Mexico's coast on Wednesday, it added.

In Manzanillo, residents waded through flooded streets on Sunday morning as soldiers helped families remove water from their homes after the storm brought heavy rain overnight.
"The beds, the refrigerators, the stoves, all the furniture got wet. The whole house flooded," Cecilia Palomar told Reuters outside her home.
"My mother doesn't want to leave. We took her to my brother's, to higher ground. She's an elderly woman, but she doesn't want to leave. She doesn't want to be away from her home."
Hurricane conditions were likely already occurring within the hurricane warning area and were expected to spread northward overnight, the NHC said.
Simon was forecast to bring an additional 50mm to 100mm of rain to parts of Colima, Jalisco, Nayarit and Sinaloa through early Thursday, with isolated areas receiving up to 200mm more.
Total rainfall from the storm could reach 762mm in parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco, raising the risk of life-threatening flooding and mudslides, particularly in mountainous areas, the NHC said. Dangerous storm surge and destructive waves were also expected along parts of the coast.
Mexican authorities placed 28 municipalities across Jalisco and Colima under the highest cyclone alert level, while another 93 municipalities were under high alert, according to civil protection bulletins.
Puerto Vallarta International Airport temporarily closed, while authorities suspended non-essential activities and opened emergency shelters in threatened coastal communities.
Earlier on Sunday, President Claudia Sheinbaum urged residents of coastal communities in Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacan to remain indoors as the storm, then a Category 4 hurricane, approached the coast.
On Saturday, residents in Manzanillo had appeared largely calm despite the approaching storm, with some businesses boarding up storefronts and civil protection personnel closing beaches and urging people to stay away from the shore.
The storm comes days after Hurricane Polo struck Mexico's Baja California Peninsula as a Category 2 hurricane, knocking down trees and power poles and flooding streets.

items.title: China imposes sanctions on Paraguay, Belize ministers over Taiwan ties
items.author: Liz Lee, Ben Blanchard
items.creator: Liz Lee, Ben Blanchard
items.summary: China on Monday placed sanctions on Paraguay's communications minister and the foreign minister of Belize over their countries' ties with Taiwan, saying they were "pawns" who have smeared Beijing, drawing strong condemnation from Taipei.
items.body:
China on Monday placed sanctions on Paraguay's communications minister and the foreign minister of Belize over their countries' ties with Taiwan, saying they were "pawns" who have smeared Beijing, drawing strong condemnation from Taipei.
Paraguay and Belize are two of just 12 countries to maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan. China says Taiwan is one of its provinces with no right to the trappings of a state, a view Taipei's government strongly rejects.
The sanctions are largely symbolic because ministers from Taiwan's diplomatic allies generally do not travel to China. Beijing has previously imposed similar measures mainly on Western politicians for their support of democratically governed Taiwan.
Paraguay's minister of information and communication technologies, Gustavo Villate, told local media on Monday the move was "to be expected," given the projects Paraguay and Taiwan are pursuing together, including a data center.
"We are very calm. We will continue working on all the projects we have and we will push this even more strongly," Villate said.
Belize's Foreign Ministry rejected the sanctions, saying measures against Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca for carrying out what it described as the "lawful duties of his office" were "unwarranted."
"These measures will not alter Belize's foreign policy, nor will they deter the Government from carrying out its responsibilities," the ministry said in a statement, adding that Belize remained fully committed to its relationship with Taiwan.
Taiwan's Foreign Ministry condemned the move, saying China had no right to interfere in its diplomatic relations.
The sanctions constitute a "blatant interference in the sovereignty and foreign policies of other nations," the ministry said in a statement.
China's Foreign Ministry cited national sovereignty and security as reasons for the measures, saying some politicians in Belize and Paraguay have been "anti-China" in pushing for their nations to maintain diplomatic ties with Taiwan.
The measures include denying entry visas for Hong Kong and Macau, and prohibiting Chinese organizations and individuals from engaging in transactions, cooperation or other activities, the ministry said in two notices.
Belize Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca met his Taiwan counterpart, Lin Chia-lung, in Belize last month. In June, Villate met Taiwan Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi in Paraguay.
BEIJING DEFENDS SANCTIONS Speaking in Beijing, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said the politicians were "willing to serve as pawns" for Taiwan.
"They have seriously interfered in China's internal affairs, spread false information about Chinese cyberattacks, and attacked and smeared China, causing a bad international impact," she added, without elaborating.
The remaining countries with ties to Taiwan should not be "repeatedly manipulated by Taiwan independence separatist forces," she said.
Shortly before the Chinese announcement, the Belize Embassy in Taiwan posted on its Facebook page a message celebrating the 37th anniversary, on October 11, of the establishment of ties between the two governments.
"Together, we look forward to a future of growth, opportunity, and lasting friendship," the embassy wrote.
China has stepped up pressure on Taiwan's remaining diplomatic allies to sever ties with Taipei.
The last country to do so was the tiny Pacific Island nation of Nauru, in 2024. Honduras ended its decades-long ties with Taiwan in 2023.

US Republicans, Democrats want Trump to reverse course on Russia diesel

Donald Trump's administration failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation of its decision, something required by law, seven senators said.

U.S. Senator Thom Tillis (R-NC) attends the committee vote on U.S. President Donald Trump's nomination of Todd Blanche to be U.S. attorney general, on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., U.S., August 4, 2026. REUTERS/Elizabeth Frantz

Republican and Democratic US senators called on President Donald Trump on Sunday (Oct 11) to "reverse course" on his diesel supply deal with Russia, saying it runs counter to US law barring imports of energy until Russia ends its aggression against Ukraine.
"Congress explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing (Russian President Vladimir) Putin’s brutal war against Ukraine," the seven senators - four of Trump's fellow Republicans and three Democrats - said in a statement.
They also said that the administration failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation of its decision, something also required by law.
"The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians. The Administration must immediately reverse course," the statement said.

It was only the latest bipartisan criticism of Trump's deal, a shift from his party's near-unanimous support for Trump's foreign policy decision weeks before Nov 3 midterm elections that will determine whether his Republicans will retain their control of Congress.
It was issued by Republican Senators Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, Thom Tillis of North Carolina and John Curtis of Utah and Democrats Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut and Ron Wyden of Oregon.
Tillis had said earlier on Sunday that the diesel deal may be illegal and would put American lives at risk.

Related:

Russia hits Ukraine power plants despite Trump energy ceasefire claim

Ukraine's Zelenskyy says he will organise elections if Russia agrees to 60-day ceasefire

Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets , and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war on Ukraine.
“I do believe there’s a legitimate case for saying the president’s not following the law,” Tillis, who is retiring from the Senate in January, told NBC's "Meet the Press."
Prices for diesel - used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking - are near record highs and could hurt Republicans in next month's congressional elections.
Analysts have said that Trump's agreement with Moscow was unlikely to lead to sustained lower fuel prices.
ADMINISTRATION DEFENDS PACT US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Sunday that the Trump administration will follow through with the deal using existing legal authority, and the agreement was good for the American people and would bring prices down.
"We're going to do it with all the legal authorities we have. So, you know, anyone in Congress who says whether it's an old bill or the current Lindsey Graham bill (that) prohibits us from doing it is wrong," Bessent told Fox & Friends.
Trump last month signed a sweeping Russia sanctions bill into law, called the "Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026", to honour the South Carolina Republican and longtime Russia hawk who died in July.
Some other Republicans had also criticised the diesel plan. Retiring Representative Don Bacon of Nebraska said on X on Friday that "propping up Putin's war economy is morally wrong as he uses that money to bomb cities".
Mike Pence, Trump's former vice president, called his decision to lift sanctions on Russian oil a "betrayal" of Graham’s legacy and urged the president to "rescind" it.

Related:

Trump rules out diesel export ban after European release

Trump moves to cut diesel costs with order on tax-free fuel

As Trump's poll numbers have cratered, congressional Republicans have increasingly distanced themselves from the president, on matters ranging from the conflict in Iran to the trade war with Canada.
But the Senate's No 2 Republican, John Barrasso of Wyoming, defended the diesel pact, telling CBS' Face the Nation that Trump is focused on bringing costs down.
"The president is balancing and has to make tough decisions," Barrasso said.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in a call on Sunday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made it clear that the diesel deal "is in direct opposition to the efforts of Ukraine, Canada, and our allies to create peace and stability in Europe," his office said in a statement.
In a social media post on Sunday, Trump claimed that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to what he described as an "energy ceasefire" taking effect immediately, but did not elaborate.
Zelenskyy said he was still waiting to see details of that agreement.
"Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well," Zelenskyy said on the Telegram app.
There was no word from Moscow on the announcement, which followed days of US pressure on Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Source: Reuters/ec

items.title: Dollar holds 18-month high as Gulf tension, US inflation keep investors on edge
items.author: Laura Matthews
items.creator: Laura Matthews
items.summary: The dollar held at an 18-month high on Monday, supported by safe-haven demand as attacks escalated in the Middle East over the weekend, keeping investors cautious ahead of key US inflation data later this week.
items.body:
The dollar held at an 18-month high on Monday, supported by safe-haven demand as attacks escalated in the [USN:L1N45X01E TEXT:"Middle East"] over the weekend, keeping investors cautious ahead of key US inflation data later this week.
The dollar index , which tracks the US currency against six others, was up 0.37% at 102.58, highest since April 2025.
Oil prices were volatile after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis stepped up strikes on Saudi Arabia, and two tankers were attacked over the weekend.
Brent crude futures rose 2.3% to $107.17 a barrel, nearing a two-week high. The attacks overshadowed Sunday's announcement from US President Donald Trump [USN:L1N45X021 TEXT:"about an energy ceasefire"] between Ukraine and Russia that seemed imperiled from the get-go, as Kyiv [USN:L8N45Y0FT TEXT:"accused Russia"] of violating the ceasefire overnight.
Brent crude is still nearly 45% above where it was before the US-Israeli war with Iran started.
Meanwhile, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said on Monday that the Federal Reserve should [USN:S0N44V02D TEXT:"move "relatively quickly""] to a restrictive policy to control inflation she sees as more broad based.
Investors have been increasing bullish positions on the dollar, which as of the week ended October 7 came to about $36 billion, up from $8.4 billion three weeks ago , largely at the expense of the euro.
"We aren’t convinced this latest bout of risk aversion will translate into sustained dollar strength," said Joel Kruger, market strategist at LMAX Group in London, citing cooling economic data, inflation pressures moderating, and much of the Fed's expected rate hikes already priced into the market. "We see limited scope for additional dollar upside."
SPOTLIGHT MOVES TO US INFLATION DATA Wednesday's US consumer inflation report, one of the last major economic releases before the Fed's policy meeting this month, could be critical in determining the near-term direction of the dollar.
US consumer sentiment deteriorated further in early October, as the rising cost of living because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy.
The Fed raised rates last month for the first time since 2023 to rein in inflation. Traders are pricing in a 78% chance of the Fed standing pat this month, up from 51% a month earlier, the CME FedWatch tool showed.
"The real focus is on the CPI number this week -- it is likely to be running hot," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex in New York. He added that a rate hike before an election is so uncommon that "the bar is kind of high" for the Fed to act.
Investors have grown worried about the sharp selloffs in bond markets that have driven borrowing costs across the globe to multi-decade highs.
The euro fell 0.4% to $1.1156, near a 17-month low, after clocking a fifth straight week of losses last week, driven by investor angst around France's fiscal health before the 2027 presidential election.
The spread between French 10-year yields and safer German yields traded at 140 basis points. Last week it neared 160 bps, the most since 2012.
"There's been no improvement and no real clear guidance as to what's going to make things better in the short term," said Dan Tobon, head of G10 FX strategy at Citi in New York. "What's the reason to buy European debt, to buy euro here? It's hard to find one, and so we just kind of keep drifting off."
The US dollar rose 0.2% to 158.66 yen , while the pound slipped 0.2% at $1.3203.
